translations.literal: He Qing, Shen Xiyi, Shi Bangxian
translations.idiomatic: He Qing, Shen Xiyi, and Shi Bangxian

sentences.zh: 馬永，字天錫，遷安人。

translations.literal: Ma Yong, styled Tiansi, was a man of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yong, styled Tiansi, was a native of Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 生而魁岸，驍果有謀。

translations.literal: From birth he was towering in stature, fierce and resolute, and possessed stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was imposing in stature—fierce, resolute, and full of stratagem.

sentences.zh: 習兵法，好《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He studied military manuals and loved the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He studied military manuals and loved the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職為金吾左衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office as commander of the Left Branch of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his hereditary post as commander of the Left Branch of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 正德時，從陸完擊賊有功，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era he followed Lu Wan in attacking bandits with merit and was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he followed Lu Wan in fighting rebels with distinction and was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 江彬練兵西內，永當隸彬，稱疾避之。

translations.literal: When Jiang Bin drilled troops in the Western Palace, Yong was to be placed under Bin; he pleaded illness to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Bin drilled troops in the Western Palace, Yong was to be placed under his command; he pleaded illness to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 守備遵化，寇入馬蘭峪，參將陳乾被劾，擢永代。

translations.literal: As garrison commander at Zunhua, when bandits entered Mala Pass, Assistant Commander Chen Qian was impeached and Yong was promoted to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as garrison commander at Zunhua, bandits entered Mala Pass; Assistant Commander Chen Qian was impeached, and Yong was promoted to replace him.

sentences.zh: 戰柏崖、白羊峪，皆有功。

translations.literal: In battles at Baiya and Baiyang Ravine he had merit each time.
translations.idiomatic: In fighting at Baiya and Baiyang Ravine he won merit on each occasion.

sentences.zh: 十三年進都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮守薊州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Junior Grand Mentor, appointed supreme commander, and garrisoned Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to junior grand mentor, appointed supreme commander, and posted to garrison Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 盡汰諸營老弱，聽其農賈，取備直給健卒，由是永所將獨雄於諸鎮。

translations.literal: He completely eliminated the old and weak from all camps, allowed them to farm or trade, took reserve-pay funds and gave them to sturdy soldiers; thus the troops Yong commanded alone were strongest among all garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared out the old and weak from every camp, let them farm or trade, redirected reserve pay to his able-bodied troops, and so the force under Yong alone outmatched every other garrison.

sentences.zh: 武宗至喜峰口，欲出塞，永叩馬諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong reached Xifeng Pass and wished to go beyond the border, Yong seized his horse's reins and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong reached Xifeng Pass and wished to ride beyond the border, Yong seized his horse's reins and remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝註視久之，笑而止。

translations.literal: The emperor stared at him a long while, then smiled and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fixed his gaze on him for a long while, then smiled and gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 中路擦崖當敵沖，無城堡，耕牧者輒被掠。

translations.literal: The central route at Caya faced the enemy thrust; there was no fortress, and those who farmed or herded were often raided.
translations.idiomatic: The central route at Caya lay in the enemy's path; there was no fortress, and farmers and herders were constantly raided.

sentences.zh: 永令人持一月糧，營崖表，版築其內。

translations.literal: Yong had men carry a month's rations, camp on the cliff face, and build an earthen wall within.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had men carry a month's rations, camp on the cliff face, and build an earthen rampart within.

sentences.zh: 城廨如期立，乃遷軍守之。

translations.literal: The walled compound was completed on schedule, and he then transferred troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The walled compound was finished on schedule, and he then moved troops in to hold it.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進署都督同知。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to Acting Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to acting commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，金山礦盜作亂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, bandits rose at the Jinshan mines.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing, bandits rose up at the Jinshan mines.

sentences.zh: 遣指揮康雄討平之，塞其礦。

translations.literal: He sent Commander Kang Xiong to suppress and pacify them and sealed the mines.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commander Kang Xiong to suppress them, restored order, and sealed the mines shut.

sentences.zh: 朵顏把兒孫結諸部邀賞不得，盜邊。

translations.literal: Ba'er's grandson of the Tumed united various tribes when their demand for rewards was denied and raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Ba'er's grandson of the Tumed united various tribes when their demand for rewards was refused, then raided the border.

sentences.zh: 永迎擊洪山口，而伏兵斷其後，斬獲過當，進右都督。

translations.literal: Yong met them at Hongshankou while ambush troops cut off their rear; the kills and captures were excessive; he was promoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yong met them at Hongshankou while ambush troops cut off their retreat; kills and captures far exceeded the norm, and he was promoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 已，復馘其驍將，把兒孫不敢復擾邊。

translations.literal: Later he again beheaded their fierce commander, and Ba'er's grandson dared not again harass the border.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again beheaded their fiercest commander, and Ba'er's grandson dared not trouble the border again.

sentences.zh: 大同兵變，殺巡撫張文錦，命桂勇為總兵官往鎮，而議將撫之。

translations.literal: When the Datong troops mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin, Gui Yong was appointed supreme commander to pacify the region, while the court debated pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong army mutinied and killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin, Gui Yong was appointed supreme commander to take charge of the region, while the court debated whether to pacify the rebels.

sentences.zh: 永言：「逆賊幹紀，朝廷赦其脅從，恩至渥也，顧猶抗命。

translations.literal: Yong said: "The rebels have violated discipline. The court has pardoned those who were coerced—grace already overflowing—yet they still resist orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "These rebels have violated discipline. The court has already pardoned those who were coerced—grace could hardly be greater—yet they still defy orders.

sentences.zh: 今不剿，春和北寇南牧，叛卒勾連，禍滋大。

translations.literal: If they are not exterminated now, in spring the northern barbarians will drive south to pasture, and the mutineers will collude with them—the calamity will grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not exterminate them now, in spring the northern barbarians will drive their herds south, the mutineers will collude with them, and the disaster will only grow.

sentences.zh: 宜亟調鄰鎮兵，克期攻城，曉譬利害，懸破格之賞，令賊自相斬為功，元兇不難殄也。

translations.literal: Neighboring garrison troops should be hurriedly mobilized, a date set for storming the city, the harm and benefit explained clearly, and extraordinary rewards posted so that the rebels would slay one another for merit—the ringleaders would not be hard to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring garrisons should be mobilized at once, a date fixed for storming the city, the stakes explained plainly, and extraordinary rewards posted so the rebels would cut one another down for merit—the ringleaders would not be hard to destroy.

sentences.zh: 」乃命永督諸軍與侍郎胡瓚往。

translations.literal: " He was then ordered to supervise all troops with Vice Minister Hu Zan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then ordered to take command of all troops and go with Vice Minister Hu Zan.

sentences.zh: 會亂平，乃還鎮。

translations.literal: When the disturbance was pacified, he returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the revolt had already been pacified, and he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 永上書為陸完請恤典，且乞宥議禮獲罪諸臣。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized to request posthumous honors for Lu Wan and also begged pardon for the officials punished in the Rites Controversy.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized to request posthumous honors for Lu Wan and also begged pardon for the officials punished in the Rites Controversy.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，奪永官，寄祿南京後府。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, stripped Yong of his office, and had his salary attached at the Nanjing Rear Court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, stripped Yong of his office, and had his salary attached at the Nanjing Rear Court.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史丘養浩言：「永仁以恤軍，廉以律已，固邊防，卻強敵，軍民安堵，資彼長城。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Qiu Yanghao said: "Yong is benevolent in comforting the troops, incorrupt in restraining himself, solid in frontier defense, and repelling strong enemies; soldiers and civilians live in peace, relying on him as the long wall.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Qiu Yanghao said, "Yong is benevolent in comforting the troops, incorrupt in restraining himself, steadfast in frontier defense, and resolute against strong enemies; soldiers and civilians live in peace, relying on him as their long wall.

sentences.zh: 聞永去，遮道乞留，且攜子女欲遂逃移。

translations.literal: When it was learned Yong was leaving, they blocked the road begging him to stay, and some even brought their wives and children intending to flee with him.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Yong was leaving, people blocked the road begging him to stay, and some even brought their wives and children, ready to flee with him.

sentences.zh: 夫陸完久死炎瘴，非有權勢可托。

translations.literal: Lu Wan had long died in the malarial south and had no power to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan had long since died in the malarial south and had no power left to rely on.

sentences.zh: 永徒感國士知，欲救區區之報。

translations.literal: Yong merely felt gratitude for a true minister's trust and wished to repay a small kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was moved only by a true minister's regard for him and wished to repay a small debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 不負知己，寧負國家？

translations.literal: Would he not betray his intimate friend rather than betray the state?
translations.idiomatic: Would he betray his intimate friend rather than betray the state?

sentences.zh: 祈曲賜優容，俾還鎮。

translations.literal: He begged a special indulgence and permission to return to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He begged a special indulgence and permission for Yong to return to his garrison.

sentences.zh: 」順天巡撫劉澤及給事、御史交章救之，俱被譴。

translations.literal: " Shuntian Grand Coordinator Liu Ze and various remonstrance officials and censors presented memorials in his defense, all of whom were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuntian Grand Coordinator Liu Ze and various remonstrance officials and censors presented memorials in his defense, and all were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 永竟廢不用。

translations.literal: Yong was ultimately dismissed and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was ultimately dismissed and never employed again.

sentences.zh: 永杜門讀書，清約如寒士。

translations.literal: Yong shut his doors and read books, living plainly like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Yong shut his doors and devoted himself to reading, living as plainly as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 久之，用薦僉書南京前府。

translations.literal: After a long time, through recommendation he served as registrar of the Nanjing Front Court.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, on recommendation he served as registrar of the Nanjing Front Court.

sentences.zh: 大同軍再亂，廷臣交薦。

translations.literal: The Datong army rebelled again, and court officials recommended him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong army rebelled again, court officials recommended him one after another.

sentences.zh: 召至，已就撫，復還南京。

translations.literal: When summoned, the rebels had already submitted; he returned again to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned, the rebels had already submitted, and he returned once more to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遼東兵變。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Liaodong army mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the Liaodong army mutinied.

sentences.zh: 罷總兵官劉淮，以永代之。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Liu Huai was dismissed and Yong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Liu Huai was dismissed, and Yong was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 大清堡守將徐顥誘殺泰寧衛九人。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Xu Hao at Daqing Fort induced the killing of nine men of the Taiping Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao, the garrison commander at Daqing Fort, induced the killing of nine men of the Taiping Guard.

sentences.zh: 部長把當孩怒，寇邊，永擊斬之。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Badanghai was enraged and raided the border; Yong attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chief Badanghai was enraged and raided the border; Yong attacked and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 其族屬把孫借朵顏兵報讎，復為永所卻。

translations.literal: His clansman Basun borrowed Tumed troops to avenge him and was again repelled by Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Basun borrowed Tumed troops to avenge him and was again driven back by Yong.

sentences.zh: 已，復入犯。

translations.literal: Later he invaded again.
translations.idiomatic: Later they invaded again.

sentences.zh: 中官王永戰敗，永坐戴罪。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Yong was defeated in battle, and Yong was punished with demerit on his record.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Yong was defeated in battle, and Yong was punished by having to atone for the offense.

sentences.zh: 遼東自軍變後，首惡雖誅，漏綱者眾。

translations.literal: Since the military disturbance in Liaodong, though the chief culprits were executed, many escaped the net.
translations.idiomatic: Since the military disturbance in Liaodong, though the chief culprits were executed, many escaped the net.

sentences.zh: 悍卒無所憚，結黨叫呼，動懷不逞。

translations.literal: Fierce soldiers had nothing to fear; they formed factions and shouted, and often harbored reckless designs.
translations.idiomatic: Hard-bitten soldiers had nothing to fear; they formed factions, shouted defiance, and often harbored reckless designs.

sentences.zh: 廣寧卒佟伏、張鑒等乘旱饑，倡眾為亂，諸營軍憚永無應者。

translations.literal: Guangning soldiers Tong Fu and Zhang Jian and others, taking advantage of drought and famine, led the masses in revolt, but troops in the camps feared Yong and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Guangning soldiers Tong Fu, Zhang Jian, and others, taking advantage of drought and famine, stirred the masses to revolt, but troops in the other camps feared Yong and none joined them.

sentences.zh: 伏等登譙樓，鳴鼓大噪，永率家眾仰攻。

translations.literal: Fu and the others ascended a watchtower, beat drums and made a great clamor; Yong led his household retainers to attack from below.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his followers climbed a watchtower, beat drums, and raised a great clamor; Yong led his household retainers in an assault from below.

sentences.zh: 千戶張斌被殺，永戰益力，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Thousand-commander Zhang Bin was killed, but Yong fought all the harder and annihilated them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-commander Zhang Bin was killed, but Yong fought all the harder and annihilated them completely.

sentences.zh: 事聞，進左都督。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was promoted to Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, he was promoted to left commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 永畜士百余人，皆西北健兒，驍勇敢戰。

translations.literal: Yong kept more than a hundred trained men, all hardy fellows from the northwest, fierce and brave in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept more than a hundred trained men, all hardy fighters from the northwest—fierce and bold in battle.

sentences.zh: 遼東變初定，帝問將於李時。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong disturbance was first pacified, the emperor asked about generals at Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong disturbance was first pacified, the emperor asked Li Shi whom to appoint as general.

sentences.zh: 時薦永，且曰：「其家眾足用也。

translations.literal: Shi recommended Yong and said: "His household retainers are sufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: Shi recommended Yong and said, "His household retainers are more than sufficient for the task.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「將須文武兼，寧專恃勇乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "A general must combine civil and martial ability—can one rely on courage alone?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "A general must combine civil and martial ability—can one rely on courage alone?

sentences.zh: 」時曰：「遼土新定，須有威力者鎮之。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "The Liaodong territory has only just been pacified; one who has authority and might is needed to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "Liaodong has only just been pacified; a man of real authority and force is needed to hold it.

sentences.zh: 」至是，竟得其力。

translations.literal: " At this point, he indeed got his force.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end, he indeed got his force.

sentences.zh: 都御史王廷相言：「永善用兵，且廉潔，宜仍用之薊鎮，作京師藩屏。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang said: "Yong is skilled in using troops and moreover incorrupt; he should still be employed at the Jizhou garrison as a screen for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang said, "Yong is skilled in the use of troops and moreover incorrupt; he should still be employed at the Jizhou garrison as a bulwark for the capital.

sentences.zh: 」未及調，卒。

translations.literal: " Before the transfer could be made, he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before the transfer could be made, he died.

sentences.zh: 遼人為罷市。

translations.literal: The people of Liaodong closed the markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liaodong closed their markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 喪過蘇州，州人亦灑泣。

translations.literal: When his funeral passed through Suzhou, the people there also wept.
translations.idiomatic: When his funeral cortège passed through Suzhou, the townspeople wept as well.

sentences.zh: 兩鎮並立祠。

translations.literal: In both garrisons temples were erected jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In both garrisons temples were erected in his honor.

sentences.zh: 永為將，厚撫間諜，得敵人情偽，故戰輒勝。

translations.literal: As a general Yong generously paid spies and obtained the enemy's true and false intelligence, so in battle he usually won.
translations.idiomatic: As a general Yong generously paid his spies and learned the enemy's true intentions and deceptions, so in battle he usually prevailed.

sentences.zh: 雅知人，所拔卒校，後多至大帥。

translations.literal: He was skilled at recognizing talent; the soldiers and officers he promoted mostly later reached supreme command.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen eye for talent; many of the soldiers and officers he promoted later rose to supreme command.

sentences.zh: 尚書鄭曉稱永與梁震有古良將風。

translations.literal: Minister Zheng Xiao said Yong and Liang Zhen had the air of ancient good generals.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Xiao said that Yong and Liang Zhen had the bearing of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 梁震，新野人。

translations.literal: Liang Zhen was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhen was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 襲榆林衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited the office of commander of the Yulin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary post of commander of the Yulin Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年進署都指揮僉事，協守寧夏興武營。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was promoted to Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief and jointly garrisoned the Xingwu Camp in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and jointly garrisoned the Xingwu Camp in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋充延綏遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he served as roaming commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as roaming commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 廉勇，好讀兵書，善訓士，力挽強命中，數先登。

translations.literal: Incorrupt and brave, he loved reading military books, was skilled at training troops, could draw a strong bow with accurate shots, and often led the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt and brave, he loved reading military books, was skilled at training troops, could draw a heavy bow with unerring aim, and often led the assault.

sentences.zh: 擢延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Supreme Commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy supreme commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 與總兵官王效卻敵鎮遠關，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Together with Supreme Commander Wang Xiao he repelled the enemy at Zhenyuan Pass and was promoted to Junior Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Supreme Commander Wang Xiao he repelled the enemy at Zhenyuan Pass and was promoted to junior grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 吉囊、俺答犯延綏，震敗之黃甫川。

translations.literal: Jirong and Altan invaded Yan-sui; Zhen defeated them at Huangfu River.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong and Altan invaded Yan-sui; Zhen defeated them at Huangfu River.

sentences.zh: 尋犯響水、波羅，參將任傑大敗之。

translations.literal: Soon they invaded Xiangshui and Boluo; Assistant Commander Ren Jie greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they invaded Xiangshui and Boluo, where Assistant Commander Ren Jie inflicted a crushing defeat on them.

sentences.zh: 吉囊復以十萬騎入寇，震大破之幹溝，獲首功百余。

translations.literal: Jirong again invaded with a hundred thousand horsemen; Zhen utterly defeated them at Ganhogou, taking more than a hundred heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong again invaded with a hundred thousand horsemen; Zhen routed them at Ganhogou and took more than a hundred heads for merit.

sentences.zh: 先後被獎賚。

translations.literal: He was rewarded time and again.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded again and again.

sentences.zh: 已，增俸一等。

translations.literal: Later his salary was increased one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Later his salary was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 幹溝凡三十里，當敵沖。

translations.literal: Ganhogou was thirty li in all and faced the enemy thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Ganhogou stretched thirty li and lay directly in the enemy's path.

sentences.zh: 震浚使深廣，築土墻其上，寇不復輕犯。

translations.literal: Zhen had the moat dug deeper and wider and built an earthen wall atop it, so the enemy no longer lightly violated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had the moat dug deeper and wider and built an earthen wall above it, so the enemy no longer ventured to violate it lightly.

sentences.zh: 十四年進都督同知，充陜西總兵官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief and appointed supreme commander of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief and appointed supreme commander of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋論黃甫川功，進右都督。

translations.literal: Soon for his merit at Huangfu River he was promoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his merit at Huangfu River, he was promoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮大同。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 大同亂兵連殺巡撫張文錦、總兵官李瑾。

translations.literal: Datong's mutinous soldiers in succession killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin and Supreme Commander Li Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Datong's mutinous soldiers in succession killed Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin and Supreme Commander Li Jin.

sentences.zh: 繼瑾者魯綱，威不振，兵益驕，文武大吏不敢要束。

translations.literal: Lu Gang followed Jin, but his authority did not flourish; the troops grew more arrogant, and civil and military superiors dared not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gang followed Jin as supreme commander, but his authority never took hold; the troops grew more arrogant, and civil and military superiors dared not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 廷議以為憂，移震往。

translations.literal: The court deliberation regarded it as worry; Zhen was transferred there.
translations.idiomatic: The court viewed the situation with alarm and transferred Zhen to Datong.

sentences.zh: 震素畜健兒五百人，至則下令軍中，申約束。

translations.literal: Zhen had always kept five hundred stalwart soldiers; upon arriving he issued orders in the army and proclaimed discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had long maintained a corps of five hundred crack troops; upon arrival he issued orders throughout the army and enforced discipline.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵素憚震，由是帖服。

translations.literal: The garrison troops had always feared Zhen; thereby they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops had long feared Zhen, and thus submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，震破之牛心山，斬級百余。

translations.literal: Bandits entered and invaded; Zhen defeated them at Niuxin Mountain, severing more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits invaded, Zhen defeated them at Niuxin Mountain and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 寇慎，駐近邊伺隙。

translations.literal: The bandits grew cautious, encamped near the border awaiting an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits grew wary and camped near the border, waiting for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 時車駕祀山陵，震伏將士於諸路。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage worshipped at the mountain tombs; Zhen hid troops on the various routes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was performing rites at the imperial tombs; Zhen laid ambushes with troops along the roads.

sentences.zh: 寇果入，大破之宣寧灣，又破之紅崖兒，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed entered; he utterly defeated them at Xuanning Bay, again defeated them at Hongya'er, killing and capturing in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits entered as expected; he routed them at Xuanning Bay and again at Hongya'er, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，蔭一子百戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Commander-in-Chief; one son was ennobled as hundred-household commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left commander-in-chief, and one son was granted hereditary ennoblement as a hundred-household commandant.

sentences.zh: 震父棟，前陣亡。

translations.literal: Zhen's father Dong had earlier died in battle in the front lines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Dong had previously fallen in battle.

sentences.zh: 震辭蔭子，乞父祭葬，帝喜而許之。

translations.literal: Zhen declined ennobling his son, begged to perform rites and burial for his father; the emperor was pleased and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen declined the ennoblement for his son and petitioned instead to perform the sacrificial rites and burial for his father; the emperor was pleased and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 毛伯溫督師，與震修鎮邊諸堡，不數月工成。

translations.literal: Mao Bowen supervised the army; together with Zhen he repaired the various border garrison forts, and within months the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bowen took command of the forces, and together with Zhen repaired the border garrison forts; the work was completed within a few months.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，賜其家銀幣，加贈太保，謚武壯。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, silver and coins given his family, additionally granted Grand Preceptor, posthumous title Wuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title of grand tutor of the crown prince; his family received silver and coins, he was further granted grand preceptor, and given the posthumous name Wuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 震有機略，號令明審。

translations.literal: Zhen had stratagem, and his commands were clear and precise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was resourceful in strategy, and his commands were clear and firm.

sentences.zh: 前後百十戰，未嘗少挫。

translations.literal: Before and after, in a hundred and ten battles, he never suffered the slightest setback.
translations.idiomatic: Over the course of more than a hundred battles, he never once suffered a serious setback.

sentences.zh: 時率健兒出塞劫敵營，或議其啟釁。

translations.literal: At times he led stalwart soldiers beyond the border to raid enemy camps; some debated that he was provoking hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes led his crack troops beyond the border to raid enemy camps, and some criticized this as provoking hostilities.

sentences.zh: 震曰：「凡啟釁者，謂寇不擾邊，我橫挑邀功也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Generally, what is called provoking hostilities means the bandits are not disturbing the border, yet we recklessly provoke to seek merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Provoking hostilities means the bandits are not harassing the border, yet we recklessly pick a fight to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 今數深入，乃不思一挫之耶？

translations.literal: Now they repeatedly penetrate deep—are we not to think of giving them one setback?"
translations.idiomatic: They raid deep into our territory again and again—should we not at least try to deal them one blow?"

sentences.zh: 」震歿，健兒無所歸。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, the stalwart soldiers had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen died, his crack troops were left with nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 守臣以聞，編之伍，邊將猶頗得其力。

translations.literal: The garrison official reported it; they were enrolled in military units, and border generals still obtained considerable service from them.
translations.idiomatic: The local commander reported this to the court; the men were enrolled in regular units, and border generals still found them quite useful.

sentences.zh: 代震者遼東祝雄，起家世蔭。

translations.literal: To replace Zhen was Zhu Xiong of Liaodong, who rose through hereditary ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's successor was Zhu Xiong of Liaodong, who had risen through hereditary ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 歷都督僉事。

translations.literal: He served as Junior Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of junior grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 自山西副總兵遷鎮大同。

translations.literal: From deputy supreme commander of Shanxi he was transferred to garrison Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from deputy supreme commander of Shanxi to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 被劾解職，起鎮薊州。

translations.literal: Impeached and relieved of office, he was recalled to garrison Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After being impeached and dismissed, he was later recalled to garrison Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 善撫士，治軍肅。

translations.literal: Skilled at comforting troops, administering the army with strictness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning over his men and ran a disciplined army.

sentences.zh: 寇入塞，率子弟為士卒先。

translations.literal: When bandits entered the pass, he led his sons and younger relatives ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raided across the border, he led his sons and kin at the head of the troops.

sentences.zh: 子少卻，行法不貸。

translations.literal: When a son retreated slightly, he enforced the law without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When one of his sons fell slightly back, he enforced military law without exception.

sentences.zh: 世宗書其名禦屏。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor wrote his name on the imperial screen.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor had his name inscribed on the imperial screen.

sentences.zh: 為將三十年，布袍氈笠，不異卒伍。

translations.literal: As a general for thirty years, he wore cotton robes and felt hats, no different from common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years as a general he wore cotton robes and a felt hat, no different from the common rank and file.

sentences.zh: 既歿，遺貲僅供殮具。

translations.literal: After his death, his remaining property barely sufficed for burial goods.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his estate barely covered the cost of his coffin and burial.

sentences.zh: 薊人祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Ji enshrined and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jizhou erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 王效，延綏人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiao was a man of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiao was a native of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 讀書能文辭，嫻韜略。

translations.literal: In reading books he could compose literary phrasing; he was versed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read and skilled with language, and versed in military strategy.

sentences.zh: 騎射絕人，中武會試。

translations.literal: In mounted archery he surpassed others; he passed the military metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: His horsemanship and archery were unmatched, and he passed the military metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累官都指揮僉事，充延綏右參將。

translations.literal: In Jiajing, he cumulatively reached Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief and served as right assistant commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he rose to acting assistant commander-in-chief and served as right assistant commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 出神木塞，搗寇雙乃山，斬獲多。

translations.literal: Exiting Shenmu Pass, he raided the bandits at Shuannai Mountain, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: Sortieing from Shenmu Pass, he struck the bandits at Shuannai Mountain and took many heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 尋擢延綏副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Deputy Supreme Commander of Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to deputy supreme commander of Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，進署都督僉事，充總兵官，代周尚文鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, winter, he was promoted to Acting Junior Grand Mentor, appointed supreme commander, replacing Zhou Shangwen to garrison Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year he was promoted to acting junior grand mentor, appointed supreme commander, and replaced Zhou Shangwen as garrison commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 吉囊犯鎮遠關，效與梁震敗之柳門。

translations.literal: Jirong violated Zhenyuan Pass; Xiao together with Liang Zhen defeated him at Liumen.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong attacked Zhenyuan Pass; Xiao and Liang Zhen defeated him at Liumen.

sentences.zh: 追北蜂窩山，蹙溺之河，斬首百四十有奇。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Fengwo Mountain, he pressed them into the river and drowned them, severing more than one hundred forty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them north to Fengwo Mountain, he drove them into the river and drowned them, taking more than one hundred forty heads.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎賚。

translations.literal: An imperial seal letter rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He received an imperial commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 吉囊十萬騎復窺花馬池，效、震拒之不得入，轉犯幹溝。

translations.literal: Jirong with a hundred thousand horsemen again spied on Huama Pool; Xiao and Zhen barred them from entering, so they turned to invade Ganhogou.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong returned with a hundred thousand horsemen to probe Huama Pool; Xiao and Zhen kept them from entering, so they turned to raid Ganhogou.

sentences.zh: 震分兵擊，遂趨固原。

translations.literal: Zhen divided troops to attack; they then rushed toward Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen split his forces to engage them, but the bandits then pushed toward Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 總兵官劉文力戰，寇趨青山峴，大掠安定、會寧。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Liu Wen fought fiercely; the bandits headed for Qingshan Xian and greatly plundered Anding and Huining.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Liu Wen fought hard, but the bandits pushed toward Qingshan Xian and plundered Anding and Huining on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 效方敗別部於鼠湖，追至沙湖，疾移師往援，破之安定，再破之靈州，先後斬首百五十余級。

translations.literal: Xiao had just defeated a separate band at Shuhu, pursued to Shahu; he swiftly shifted troops to aid, defeated them at Anding, again defeated them at Lingzhou, in succession severing more than one hundred fifty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao had just routed a separate band at Shuhu and pursued them to Shahu; he then rushed troops to the rescue, defeated the enemy at Anding, routed them again at Lingzhou, and in all took more than one hundred fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 總制三邊尚書唐龍以大捷聞，而巡按御史奏諸將失事罪。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of the Three Borders Minister Tang Long reported the great victory, while the touring investigating censor memorialized the generals' failures.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator of the Three Borders Tang Long reported a great victory, while the touring censor memorialized that the generals had failed in their duties.

sentences.zh: 給事中戚賢往勘，奏：「安、會二縣多殺掠，文當罪。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qi Xian went to investigate and memorialized: "An and Hui two counties suffered much killing and plundering; Wen should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qi Xian went to investigate and memorialized: "An and Huining counties suffered heavy killing and plundering, and Wen should be punished.

sentences.zh: 然麾下卒僅八千，倍道蒙險，攖八九萬方張之寇，殊死戰，宜以功贖。

translations.literal: Yet under his command troops numbered only eight thousand; marching by forced marches through danger, grappling with eighty or ninety thousand bandits at full strength in death-fighting combat—merits should redeem faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had only eight thousand men under his command; marching by forced marches through perilous terrain, they grappled with eighty or ninety thousand bandits at the height of their power and fought to the death—their merits should redeem their faults.

sentences.zh: 震幹溝，效鼠湖、沙湖、安定、靈州之戰，以孤軍八百，當寇萬余，功俱足錄。

translations.literal: At Ganhogou for Zhen, and in the battles at Shuhu, Shahu, Anding, and Lingzhou for Xiao, with a lone army of eight hundred facing more than ten thousand bandits, their merits all suffice for record.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganhogou, Zhen, and at Shuhu, Shahu, Anding, and Lingzhou, Xiao, each with a lone force of eight hundred against more than ten thousand bandits—their achievements all merit recognition.

sentences.zh: 龍亦善調度。

translations.literal: Long also was skilled at coordination.
translations.idiomatic: Long, too, had exercised good coordination.

sentences.zh: 」詔文奪職，震、效賚銀幣，龍一子入監。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Wen of office, rewarded Zhen and Xiao with silver and coins, and enrolled one of Long's sons in the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Wen of office, rewarded Zhen and Xiao with silver and coins, and enrolled one of Long's sons in the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 是役也功多，執政尼之，故賞薄。

translations.literal: This campaign had many achievements, but those in power obstructed rewards, so rewards were meager.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign achievements were many, but those in power blocked full recognition, so the rewards were meager.

sentences.zh: 御史周鈇以為言，龍、效、震各加一級，效進都督同知。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Fu spoke on it; Long, Xiao, and Zhen each gained one rank; Xiao was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Fu raised the matter; Long, Xiao, and Zhen each received a promotion of one rank, and Xiao was advanced to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋以清水營功，進右都督。

translations.literal: Soon for merit at Qingshui Camp, he was promoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his merit at Qingshui Camp, he was promoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寇以輕騎犯寧夏，效伏兵打鎧口，俟其半入橫擊，敗之，而防河卒復以戰艘邀斬其奔渡者。

translations.literal: Bandits with light cavalry violated Ningxia; Xiao hid troops at Dagaikou, waited until half had entered and struck across, defeated them, while river-defense soldiers again with warships intercepted and severed those fleeing across.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits raided Ningxia with light cavalry; Xiao ambushed them at Dagaikou, waited until half had crossed, then struck them from the flank and routed them, while river-defense troops in warships intercepted and cut down those fleeing across the water.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進左都督。

translations.literal: Victory reported, he was promoted to Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to left commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寇憤，設伏誘敗之，貶右都督。

translations.literal: The bandits, enraged, set an ambush and lured him into defeat; he was demoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, enraged, set an ambush and lured him into defeat; he was demoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十六年移鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，謚武襄。

translations.literal: After a year he died; posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died and was given the posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 效言行謹飭，用兵兼謀勇，威名著西陲。

translations.literal: Xiao in conduct and speech was strict and disciplined; in employing troops he combined stratagem and bravery; his renown was established on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was strict and disciplined in word and deed, combined strategy and courage in battle, and his fame was established on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 與馬永、梁震、周尚文並為名將。

translations.literal: Together with Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, and Zhou Shangwen he was ranked as a famed general.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked among the famed generals together with Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, and Zhou Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 劉文者，陽和衛人。

translations.literal: Liu Wen was a man of Yanghe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wen was a native of Yanghe Guard.

sentences.zh: 襲指揮同知。

translations.literal: He inherited the office of assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary post of assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 屢遷署都督僉事，涼州右副總兵。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Acting Junior Grand Mentor, right deputy supreme commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to acting junior grand mentor and right deputy supreme commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年以總兵官鎮陜西。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing as supreme commander he garrisoned Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he was appointed supreme commander and posted to garrison Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 大破洮、岷叛番若籠、板爾諸族，斬首三百六十有奇。

translations.literal: Greatly defeated the rebelling Tibetans of Tao and Min—the Ruolong, Ban'er, and other tribes—severing more than three hundred sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: He inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebelling Tibetan tribes of Tao and Min, including the Ruolong and Ban'er clans, taking more than three hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 十一年，寇西掠還，將犯寧夏河東，文擊破之。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, bandits raided west and returned, about to violate Ningxia east of the river; Wen defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year bandits raided westward and, on their return, were about to strike east of the river in Ningxia; Wen defeated them.

sentences.zh: 積前功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: Accumulating prior merit, he was promoted to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated earlier achievements, he was promoted to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 後落職，起鎮延綏，改甘肅。

translations.literal: Later dismissed from office, he was recalled to garrison Yan-sui, then transferred to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed, then recalled to garrison Yan-sui, and subsequently transferred to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 卒，亦謚武襄。

translations.literal: He died; also posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was likewise given the posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 周尚文，字彥章，西安後衛人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shangwen, styled Yanzhang, was a man of Xi'an Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shangwen, styled Yanzhang, was a native of Xi'an Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 幼讀書，粗曉大義。

translations.literal: From youth he read books and roughly understood essential principles.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he studied and gained a rough grasp of the classics.

sentences.zh: 多謀略，精騎射。

translations.literal: He had many stratagems and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was full of stratagem and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十六，襲指揮同知。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he inherited assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he inherited the post of assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 屢出塞有功，進指揮使。

translations.literal: Repeatedly going beyond the border with merit, he was promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly campaigned beyond the border with distinction and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 寘鑠反，遏黃河渡口，獲叛賊丁廣等，推掌衛事。

translations.literal: When Zhu Zhifang rebelled, he blocked the Yellow River crossing, captured rebel Ding Guang and others, and was promoted to manage guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Zhifang rebelled, he sealed the Yellow River crossing, captured the rebels Ding Guang and others, and was promoted to take charge of guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 關內回賊四起，倚南山，尚文次第平之。

translations.literal: Within the passes Hui bandits rose in all quarters, relying on the southern mountains; Shangwen in succession pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebels rose throughout the interior, sheltering in the southern mountains; Shangwen pacified them one after another.

sentences.zh: 御史劉天和劾中貴廖堂系詔獄，事連尚文。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tianhe impeached the court eunuch Liao Tang and had him imprisoned by imperial command; the matter implicated Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Tianhe impeached the eunuch Liao Tang and had him imprisoned by imperial order; the case implicated Shangwen as well.

sentences.zh: 拷掠令引天和，終不承，久之始釋。

translations.literal: Under torture he was ordered to implicate Tianhe, but he never confessed; only after a long while was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he was ordered to implicate Tianhe, but he never confessed; only after a long time was he released.

sentences.zh: 已，守備階州。

translations.literal: Later, garrison commander at Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as garrison commander at Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 計擒叛番，進署都指揮僉事，充甘肅遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Through stratagem he captured rebelling Tibetans; promoted to Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief, serving as Gansu roaming commander.
translations.idiomatic: By stratagem he captured rebelling Tibetans and was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief, serving as roaming commander of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年改寧夏參將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was changed to Ningxia assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred to serve as assistant commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 尋進都指揮同知，為涼州副總兵。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief, becoming deputy supreme commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief and appointed deputy supreme commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史按部莊浪，猝遇寇。

translations.literal: A censor was inspecting Zhuanglang when suddenly encountering bandits.
translations.idiomatic: While a censor was on inspection tour in Zhuanglang, bandits suddenly appeared.

sentences.zh: 尚文亟分軍擁御史，而自引麾下射之，寇乃遁。

translations.literal: Shangwen urgently divided troops to protect the censor, while personally leading his men to shoot at them; the bandits then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen quickly split his forces to shield the censor, while personally leading his men to drive the bandits off with arrows.

sentences.zh: 嘗追寇出塞，寇來益眾。

translations.literal: Once pursuing bandits beyond the border, the bandits came increasingly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while pursuing bandits beyond the border, the enemy forces grew ever larger.

sentences.zh: 尚文軍半至，麾下皆恐。

translations.literal: Shangwen's army had only half arrived; all under his command were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Only half of Shangwen's force had come up, and his men were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 乃從容下馬，解鞍背崖力戰，所殺傷相當。

translations.literal: He then calmly dismounted, removed the saddle, fought with his back to the cliff with full strength; the killed and wounded were comparable.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly dismounted, fought with his back against the cliff, and casualties were roughly even on both sides.

sentences.zh: 部將丁杲來援，寇始退。

translations.literal: Assistant General Ding Gao came to aid; the bandits then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant General Ding Gao arrived with reinforcements, and the bandits finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尚文被創甚，乃告歸。

translations.literal: Shangwen was wounded severely; he then requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen was badly wounded and requested leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 尋起故官。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 吉囊數踏冰入。

translations.literal: Jirong many times trod ice to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong repeatedly crossed the frozen river to raid.

sentences.zh: 尚文築墻百二十里，澆以水，冰滑不可上。

translations.literal: Shangwen built a wall one hundred twenty li, poured water on it; the ice was slippery and could not be climbed.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen built a wall one hundred twenty li long and poured water over it; when it froze the surface was too slick to climb.

sentences.zh: 冰泮則令力士持長竿鐵鉤，鉤殺渡者。

translations.literal: When the ice melted he ordered strongmen holding long poles with iron hooks to hook and kill those crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the ice broke up he had strongmen with long poles and iron hooks hook and kill those attempting to cross.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢署都督僉事，充寧夏總兵官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Acting Junior Grand Mentor and appointed Ningxia supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to acting junior grand mentor and appointed supreme commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 王瓊築邊墻，尚文督其役。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong built the border wall; Shangwen supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qiong built the border wall, Shangwen supervised the work.

sentences.zh: 且浚渠開屯，軍民利之。

translations.literal: Moreover he dredged canals and opened military colonies; troops and people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged canals and opened military colonies, to the benefit of troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 寇掠西海，過寧夏，巡撫楊誌學議發兵邀。

translations.literal: Bandits plundered Xihai, passed Ningxia; Grand Coordinator Yang Zhixue proposed dispatching troops to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raided Xihai and passed through Ningxia, Grand Coordinator Yang Zhixue proposed sending troops to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 尚文不從，劾解職。

translations.literal: Shangwen did not comply; he was impeached and relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen refused; he was impeached and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，起山西副總兵。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was recalled as deputy supreme commander of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as deputy supreme commander of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 寇由偏頭關趨岢嵐，尚文轉戰三百里，破之，與子君佐俱傷，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Bandits from Piantou Pass headed toward Kelan; Shangwen fought turning battles three hundred li and defeated them; together with his son Junzuo he was wounded, and was rewarded with silver and coins.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came from Piantou Pass toward Kelan, Shangwen fought them over three hundred li and routed them; he and his son Junzuo were both wounded, and he was rewarded with silver and coins.

sentences.zh: 尋以總兵官鎮延綏。

translations.literal: Soon as supreme commander he garrisoned Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed supreme commander and posted to garrison Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 寇犯紅山墩，力戰敗之，被賚。

translations.literal: Bandits violated Hongshan Beacon; he fought with full strength and defeated them, and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked Hongshan Beacon, he fought hard and routed them, and was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 吉囊復大掠清平堡，坐奪俸。

translations.literal: Jirong again greatly plundered Qingping Fort; for this his salary was forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong again raided Qingping Fort on a large scale, and Shangwen was penalized by salary forfeiture.

sentences.zh: 尚文優將才，負氣桀傲，所至與文吏競。

translations.literal: Shangwen excelled in generalship, bore a proud and overbearing temperament, and wherever he went competed with civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen was an outstanding commander, proud and overbearing, and everywhere he went he clashed with civil officials.

sentences.zh: 文吏又往往挫折之，以故彌不相得。

translations.literal: Civil officials also often thwarted him; for this reason they became all the more incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials in turn often checked him, so the two sides grew ever more at odds.

sentences.zh: 巡撫賈啟劾尚文老誖，兵部請調之甘肅。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Jia Qi impeached Shangwen as aged and perverse; the Ministry of War requested transferring him to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Jia Qi impeached Shangwen as aged and obstinate, and the Ministry of War asked that he be transferred to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，各奪其俸。

translations.literal: The emperor did not comply; each had his salary forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree, and both men had their salaries forfeited.

sentences.zh: 巡按張光祖言兩人必不可共處，乃革尚文任，亦貶啟秩。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Zhang Guangzu said the two men absolutely could not coexist; thereupon Shangwen's appointment was revoked, and Qi's rank was also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Zhang Guangzu said the two could not possibly serve together; Shangwen was dismissed from office and Qi's rank was reduced as well.

sentences.zh: 吉囊大入，抵固原。

translations.literal: Jirong invaded on a large scale and reached Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong launched a major invasion and pushed as far as Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 天和時已為總督，激尚文立功。

translations.literal: Tianhe at the time was already governor-general; he urged Shangwen to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe was already governor-general by then and urged Shangwen to win distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 奮擊之黑水苑，殺其子號小十王者，獲首功百三十余。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely against them at Heishui Park, killed his son called the Little Ten Kings, and took more than one hundred thirty heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought fiercely at Heishui Park, killed Jirong's son known as the Little Ten Kings, and took more than one hundred thirty heads for merit.

sentences.zh: 乃以為都督同知。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Assistant Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to assistant commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，用薦為東官廳聽征總兵官兼僉後府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, on recommendation he became campaigning supreme commander of the Eastern Official Hall and concurrently signed Rear Court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, on recommendation he was appointed campaigning supreme commander of the Eastern Official Hall and concurrently placed in charge of Rear Court affairs.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩為禮部尚書，子世蕃官後府都事，驕蹇。

translations.literal: Yan Song was Minister of Rites; his son Shifan held office as Rear Court director and was arrogant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song was Minister of Rites, and his son Shifan served as director of the Rear Court in an arrogant and overbearing manner.

sentences.zh: 尚文面叱，將劾奏之，嵩謝得免。

translations.literal: Shangwen rebuked him to his face and was about to impeach and memorialize against him; Song apologized and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen rebuked him to his face and was about to impeach him, but Song apologized and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 調世蕃治中，以避尚文，銜次骨。

translations.literal: Shifan was transferred to managing director to avoid Shangwen; he bore a grudge to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was transferred to managing director to keep him away from Shangwen, and he nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 其秋以總兵官鎮大同，請增餉及馬。

translations.literal: That autumn, as supreme commander he garrisoned Datong and requested increased pay and horses.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was posted as supreme commander to garrison Datong and requested additional pay and horses.

sentences.zh: 兵部言尚文陳請過當，方被詔切責，而尚文與巡撫趙錦不協，乞休，弗允，日相構。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said Shangwen's memorial requests were excessive; he had just been sternly rebuked by imperial edict, while Shangwen and Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin were incompatible; he begged to retire, was not permitted, and day by day they plotted against each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War said Shangwen's requests were excessive; he had just been sternly rebuked by imperial edict, yet he and Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin could not get along. He asked to retire and was refused, and the two men grew more hostile by the day.

sentences.zh: 御史王三聘乞移之他鎮。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Sanpin begged to transfer him to another garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Sanpin asked that Shangwen be transferred to another garrison.

sentences.zh: 廷議：大同敵沖，尚文假此避，不宜墮其奸謀。

translations.literal: Court deliberation: Datong was the enemy's main thrust; Shangwen was using this pretext to avoid it; it was not fitting to fall into his crafty scheme.
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated: Datong lay on the enemy's main line of attack, and Shangwen was using the dispute as a pretext to escape his post; the court should not fall for his scheme.

sentences.zh: 乃以錦為甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin was made Grand Coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin was instead appointed grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 吉囊數萬騎犯前衛。

translations.literal: Jirong with tens of thousands of horsemen violated the vanguard guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jirong invaded with tens of thousands of horsemen and attacked the vanguard guard.

sentences.zh: 尚文與戰黑山，殺其子滿罕歹，追至涼城。

translations.literal: Shangwen fought them at Heishan, killed his son Manhandai, and pursued to Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen fought them at Heishan, killed Jirong's son Manhandai, and pursued the enemy as far as Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 斬獲多，進右都督。

translations.literal: The kills and captures were many; he was promoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: With many kills and captures to his credit, he was promoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 已，寇由宣府逼畿甸，出大同塞而北。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, bandits from Xuanfu pressed on the capital region, passed out through the Datong passes, and headed north.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits came from Xuanfu toward the capital region, then passed through the Datong passes and withdrew northward.

sentences.zh: 尚文邀之，稍有俘獲。

translations.literal: Shangwen intercepted them and took some prisoners and booty.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen intercepted them and took some prisoners and spoils.

sentences.zh: 後寇復大舉，犯鵓鴿谷，將南下。

translations.literal: Later the bandits again came in force, violated Buge Valley, and were about to push south.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandits returned in force, entered Buge Valley, and prepared to drive south.

sentences.zh: 尚文備陽和，遣騎四出邀寇。

translations.literal: Shangwen prepared defenses at Yanghe and dispatched horsemen in all directions to intercept the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen made ready at Yanghe and sent cavalry out in every direction to intercept the bandits.

sentences.zh: 寇遁，賜敕獎勞之。

translations.literal: The bandits fled; an imperial edict was granted to commend and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits withdrew, and the emperor issued an edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 總督翁萬達議築邊墻，自宣府西陽和至大同開山口，延袤二百余裏，以屬尚文。

translations.literal: Governor-General Weng Wanda proposed building a border wall from Yanghe west of Xuanfu to Kaishankou at Datong, extending more than two hundred li, and assigning it to Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Weng Wanda proposed building a border wall from Yanghe west of Xuanfu to Kaishankou at Datong, more than two hundred li in length, and placed the work under Shangwen's command.

sentences.zh: 乃益築陽和以西至山西丫角山，凡四百余裏，敵臺千余。

translations.literal: He then additionally built from west of Yanghe to Yajiao Mountain in Shanxi, altogether more than four hundred li, with more than a thousand enemy-facing towers.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to extend construction west from Yanghe to Yajiao Mountain in Shanxi, more than four hundred li in all, with more than a thousand watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 斥屯田四萬余頃，益軍萬三千有奇。

translations.literal: He reclaimed more than forty thousand qing of colony land and added more than thirteen thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed more than forty thousand qing of garrison colony land and added more than thirteen thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，進左都督，加太子太保，永除屯稅。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit; he was promoted to Left Commander-in-Chief, additionally granted Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince, and colony tax was permanently abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his achievements, promoted him to left commander-in-chief, granted him the title of grand guardian of the crown prince, and permanently abolished the garrison colony tax.

sentences.zh: 叛人充灼召小王子寇邊，尚文偵得其使者，加太保，蔭子錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: The rebel Chongzhuo summoned the Little Prince to raid the border; Shangwen detected his messenger; he was additionally granted Grand Guardian, and his son was ennobled as hereditary thousand-household commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Chongzhuo summoned the Little Prince to raid the frontier, Shangwen intercepted his messenger. He was further granted the rank of grand guardian, and his son was ennobled as hereditary thousand-household commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，總兵官加三公者，尚文一人而已。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty, among supreme commanders granted the three grand tutor ranks, Shangwen alone.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming dynasty, Shangwen alone among supreme commanders was granted the three grand tutor ranks.

sentences.zh: 初，俺答及吉囊諸子盛強，諸邊歲受其患，大同尤甚。

translations.literal: At first, Altan and Jirong's sons were flourishing and strong; the various frontiers yearly suffered their harm, Datong especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: At first Altan and Jirong's sons were at the height of their power, and the border regions suffered from their raids year after year, Datong most of all.

sentences.zh: 自尚文蒞鎮，與總督萬達、巡撫詹榮規畫戰守備邊，民息肩者數年。

translations.literal: From the time Shangwen arrived to garrison the post, together with Governor-General Wanda and Grand Coordinator Zhan Rong he planned warfare, defense, and border preparation; the people rested their shoulders for several years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Shangwen took command, he worked with Governor-General Wanda and Grand Coordinator Zhan Rong to plan offense, defense, and frontier preparedness, and the people enjoyed several years of relief.

sentences.zh: 尚文益招叛人，孤敵勢，歸者相屬。

translations.literal: Shangwen further recruited defectors, isolated the enemy's strength, and those who returned followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen also recruited defectors to weaken the enemy, and deserters came over in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，俺答伏兵五堡旁，誘指揮顧相等出，圍之彌陀山。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, eighth month, Altan set ambush troops beside Wubao, lured Commandant Gu Xiang and others to come out, and surrounded them at Mituo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, Altan hid troops near Wubao, lured Commandant Gu Xiang and his men out, and surrounded them on Mituo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 尚文急督副總兵林椿、參將呂勇、遊擊李梅及二子君佐、君仁出塞援，圍始解。

translations.literal: Shangwen urgently directed Deputy Supreme Commander Lin Chun, Assistant Commander Lü Yong, Roaming Commander Li Mei, and his two sons Junzuo and Junren to go beyond the border in relief; only then was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen urgently sent Deputy Supreme Commander Lin Chun, Assistant Commander Lü Yong, Roaming Commander Li Mei, and his sons Junzuo and Junren beyond the border to relieve them, and the siege was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 相及指揮周奉，千戶呂愷、郝經等已陣歿。

translations.literal: Xiang, together with Commandant Zhou Feng, Thousand-Household Commanders Lü Kai, Hao Jing, and others, had already fallen in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiang, Commandant Zhou Feng, Thousand-Household Commanders Lü Kai and Hao Jing, and others had already been killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 尚文轉戰，次野口，伏突起。

translations.literal: Shangwen fought turning battles; when he halted at Yekou, ambush troops suddenly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen fought on as he withdrew, and when he reached Yekou an ambush force suddenly sprang up.

sentences.zh: 殊死戰，斬其長一人。

translations.literal: He fought a death struggle and beheaded one of their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He fought desperately and killed one of their leaders.

sentences.zh: 相持月余乃引去。

translations.literal: They faced off for more than a month before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides faced each other for more than a month before the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尚文設伏，殺其殿卒而還。

translations.literal: Shangwen set an ambush, killed their rearguard, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen laid an ambush, cut down the enemy rearguard, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尚文三子俱罪戍，至是以父功得釋。

translations.literal: Shangwen's three sons had all been sentenced to penal garrison duty; at this time, through their father's merit, they were released.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Shangwen's sons had been sentenced to penal frontier service, and now, through their father's merit, they were released.

sentences.zh: 俺答數萬騎犯宣府，萬達檄尚文大破之曹家莊。

translations.literal: Altan with tens of thousands of horsemen violated Xuanfu; Wanda dispatched orders to Shangwen, who utterly defeated them at Caojiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Altan invaded Xuanfu with tens of thousands of horsemen; Wanda ordered Shangwen into action, and he routed the enemy at Caojiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 錄功兼太子太傅，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; he was additionally made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, and rewards were increased.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded, he was granted the additional title of grand tutor of the crown prince, and he received extraordinary rewards.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 尚文清約愛士，得士死力。

translations.literal: Shangwen was frugal and loved his men, gaining from his soldiers their utmost effort even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen lived simply and cared for his men, and they served him with their lives.

sentences.zh: 善用間，知敵中曲折，故戰輒有功。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using spies, knew the twists and turns within the enemy camp, and therefore whenever he fought achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He made excellent use of spies and understood the enemy's inner workings, so he won merit in battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 自二十年後，俺答頻擾邊。

translations.literal: From after the twentieth year, Altan frequently harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: After the twentieth year Altan raided the frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 宿將王效、馬永、梁震皆前死，惟尚文存，威名最盛。

translations.literal: Veteran generals Wang Xiao, Ma Yong, and Liang Zhen had all died earlier; only Shangwen remained, and his martial renown was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran generals Wang Xiao, Ma Yong, and Liang Zhen had all died earlier; Shangwen alone remained, and his reputation was the greatest of them all.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩父子謀傾陷。

translations.literal: Yan Song and his son plotted to overthrow and ruin him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and his son plotted to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 功高，帝方籍以抗強敵，讒不得入。

translations.literal: His merit was high; the emperor was just then relying on him to resist strong enemies, and slander could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were too great; the emperor was relying on him to hold off powerful enemies, and slander could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 暨卒，格恤典不予，給事中沈束以為言。

translations.literal: When he died, posthumous honors were withheld and not granted; Supervising Secretary Shen Shu spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, posthumous honors were denied; Supervising Secretary Shen Shu remonstrated on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 嵩激帝怒，錮束詔獄。

translations.literal: Song incited the emperor's anger and had Shu imprisoned in the imperial prison by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Song provoked the emperor's anger, and Shen Shu was imprisoned by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，始贈太傅，謚武襄。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Shangwen was posthumously granted the title of grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 趙國忠，字伯進，錦州衛人，嗣指揮職。

translations.literal: Zhao Guozhong, styled Bozin, a man of Jinzhou Guard, inherited the commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guozhong, styled Bozin, was a native of Jinzhou Guard and inherited the hereditary post of commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年舉武會試，進都指揮僉事，守備叆陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the military metropolitan examination, was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief, and garrisoned Aiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he passed the military metropolitan examination, was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief, and posted to garrison Aiyang.

sentences.zh: 擢錦義右參將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right assistant commander of Jinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant commander of Jinyi.

sentences.zh: 連破敵，增秩，賜金幣，進署都督僉事，為遼東總兵官。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the enemy, gained rank, was granted gold and coins, was promoted to Acting Junior Grand Mentor, and became supreme commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories over the enemy he was promoted in rank and rewarded with gold and coins, then made acting junior grand mentor and appointed supreme commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 禦敵有功，斬級百七十有奇。

translations.literal: In repelling the enemy he had merit; heads cut numbered more than one hundred seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in repelling the enemy, taking more than one hundred seventy heads.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知，賜賚逾等。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Commander-in-Chief; rewards exceeded the norm.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant commander-in-chief and received rewards above the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 敵以八百騎從鴉鶻關入。

translations.literal: The enemy with eight hundred horsemen entered through Yahugu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy entered through Yahugu Pass with eight hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 都指揮康雲戰歿，裨將三人亦死，詔國忠戴罪立功。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander-in-Chief Kang Yun died in battle; three lieutenant generals also died; an edict ordered Guozhong to atone for the offense by establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander-in-Chief Kang Yun was killed in battle, along with three lieutenant generals; Guozhong was ordered to atone for the failure by winning merit in battle.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事被劾，命白衣視事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of an affair he was impeached and ordered to perform his duties in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was impeached for misconduct and ordered to continue in office while stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 守備張文瀚禦敵死，國忠坐解任。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Zhang Wenhan died repelling the enemy; Guozhong was penalized and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Garrison Commander Zhang Wenhan was killed repelling the enemy, Guozhong was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋起西官廳右參將，授都督僉事，提督東官廳。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as right assistant commander of the Western Official Hall, granted Junior Grand Mentor, and put in charge of the Eastern Official Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as right assistant commander of the Western Official Hall, granted the rank of junior grand mentor, and placed in command of the Eastern Official Hall.

sentences.zh: 俺答大舉犯宣府，總兵官趙卿不任戰，命國忠代之。

translations.literal: Altan invaded Xuanfu on a large scale; Supreme Commander Zhao Qing was unequal to battle; Guozhong was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Altan launched a major invasion of Xuanfu; Supreme Commander Zhao Qing proved unable to fight, and Guozhong was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至岔道，寇已為周尚文所敗，東走。

translations.literal: When he reached Chad Road, the bandits had already been defeated by Zhou Shangwen and were fleeing east.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Chad Road, the bandits had already been defeated by Zhou Shangwen and were retreating eastward.

sentences.zh: 國忠命參將孫勇率精卒逆擊於大滹沱，敗之。

translations.literal: Guozhong ordered Assistant Commander Sun Yong to lead picked troops to strike them head-on at the Great Hutuo and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong ordered Assistant Commander Sun Yong to lead elite troops in a head-on attack at the Great Hutuo and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 與尚文分道擊，寇盡走，以功受賚。

translations.literal: Together with Shangwen he struck by separate routes; the bandits all fled; for his merit he received reward.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shangwen attacked along separate routes until the bandits were driven off entirely, and he was rewarded for his merit.

sentences.zh: 復坐寇入，降俸二等。

translations.literal: Again, on account of the bandits' entry, his salary was reduced by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: He was again penalized because the bandits had broken through, and his salary was reduced by two grades.

sentences.zh: 俺答薄京師，國忠趨入衛，壁沙河北。

translations.literal: Altan pressed close to the capital; Guozhong hurried to enter in defense and fortified north of the Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan drew near the capital, Guozhong rushed to its defense and fortified his position north of the Sha River.

sentences.zh: 已，移護諸陵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, he was transferred to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to guard the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 寇騎至天壽山，見國忠陣紅門前，不敢入。

translations.literal: The bandits' horsemen reached Tianshou Mountain; seeing Guozhong's battle line before the Red Gate, they did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits' cavalry reached Tianshou Mountain and saw Guozhong drawn up in battle order before the Red Gate, they did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，再鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he again garrisoned Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was again posted to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 小王子打來孫以數萬騎寇錦州，國忠禦卻之。

translations.literal: The Little Prince Dailaisun with tens of thousands of horsemen raided Jinzhou; Guozhong repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince Dailaisun raided Jinzhou with tens of thousands of horsemen, and Guozhong drove him back.

sentences.zh: 明年入獅子口，督參將李廣等逐出塞，斬擒五十人。

translations.literal: The next year they entered Shizi Pass; he directed Assistant Commander Li Guang and others to drive them beyond the border, beheading and capturing fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they entered through Shizi Pass; he directed Assistant Commander Li Guang and others to drive them back beyond the border, killing or capturing fifty men.

sentences.zh: 寇屢入榆林堡、高臺、蛤利河。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly entered Yulin Fort, Gaotai, and Geli River.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits repeatedly raided Yulin Fort, Gaotai, and the Geli River.

sentences.zh: 先後掩擊，獲首功百五十有奇，進秩一等。

translations.literal: In succession he made surprise attacks and took more than one hundred fifty heads for merit; he advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In a series of surprise attacks he took more than one hundred fifty heads for merit and was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 尋被論罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was criticized and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 國忠善戰，射穿劄，為將有威嚴。

translations.literal: Guozhong was skilled in battle, shooting through armor plates; as a general he had dignity and authority.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was a skilled fighter who could pierce armor with his arrows, and as a commander he carried real authority.

sentences.zh: 歷兩鎮，繕亭障，練士馬，邊防賴之。

translations.literal: Having served in two garrisons, he repaired pavilions and barriers, trained soldiers and horses, and the border defense relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He served in two garrison commands, repaired fortifications, trained troops and horses, and the frontier defenses depended on him.

sentences.zh: 馬芳，字德馨，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Ma Fang, styled Dexin, a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang, styled Dexin, was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲為北寇所掠，使之牧。

translations.literal: At age ten he was captured by northern bandits and made to herd livestock.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten he was captured by northern raiders and put to herding livestock.

sentences.zh: 芳私以曲木為弓，剡矢射，俺答獵，虎虓其前，芳一發斃之。

translations.literal: Fang secretly made a bow from bent wood and whittled arrows to shoot; Altan was hunting, a tiger charged roaring before him, and Fang with one shot killed it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang secretly fashioned a bow from bent wood and whittled arrows. While Altan was out hunting, a tiger charged roaring before him, and Fang brought it down with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 乃授以良弓矢、善馬，侍左右。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given fine bow and arrows and a good horse and attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Altan then gave him a fine bow, arrows, and a good horse, and kept him in attendance.

sentences.zh: 芳陽為之用，而潛自間道亡歸。

translations.literal: Fang outwardly served him willingly, but secretly by a hidden route fled and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pretended to serve willingly, but secretly made his way home by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 周尚文鎮大同，奇之，署為隊長。

translations.literal: Zhou Shangwen garrisoned Datong, marveled at him, and appointed him squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Shangwen was garrison commander at Datong, he was impressed by Fang and appointed him squad leader.

sentences.zh: 數禦寇有功，當得官，以父貧，悉受賞以養。
