translations.literal: He repeatedly repelled bandits with merit and ought to have received office, but because his father was poor he accepted all rewards to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He won merit again and again in repelling bandits and was eligible for promotion, but because his father was poor he took every reward to support him instead.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年秋，寇犯懷柔、順義。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing, bandits violated Huairou and Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing, bandits raided Huairou and Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 芳馳斬其將，授陽和衛總旗。

translations.literal: Fang galloped forth and beheaded their general; he was appointed chief banner officer of Yanghe Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fang galloped out, killed the enemy general, and was appointed chief banner officer of Yanghe Guard.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗入威遠，伏驍騎鹽場，而以二十騎挑戰。

translations.literal: The bandits once entered Weiyuan, hid fierce horsemen at the salt fields, and with twenty horsemen offered challenge.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits once entered Weiyuan, hid crack cavalry at the salt fields, and sent twenty horsemen forward to provoke a fight.

sentences.zh: 芳知其詐，用百騎薄伏所，三分其軍銳，以次擊之。

translations.literal: Fang knew their trick; with a hundred horsemen he pressed close to the ambush site, divided his army's elite into three parts, and struck them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Fang saw through the ruse. With a hundred horsemen he closed on the ambush site, divided his best troops into three groups, and attacked in succession.

sentences.zh: 奮勇跳蕩，敵騎辟易十里，斬首凡九十級。

translations.literal: He fought with fierce courage in leaping charges; the enemy horsemen gave way for ten li; heads cut totaled ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He charged fiercely again and again, and the enemy cavalry fell back for ten li; he took ninety heads in all.

sentences.zh: 已，復禦之新平。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, he again repelled them at Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fought them off again at Xinping.

sentences.zh: 寇營野馬川，克日戰。

translations.literal: The bandits encamped at Yema River and fixed a day for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits encamped at Yema River and set a day for battle.

sentences.zh: 芳度寇且遁，急乘之，斬級益多。

translations.literal: Fang judged that the bandits would soon flee; he urgently pressed them and beheaded still more.
translations.idiomatic: Fang judged that the bandits would soon withdraw, pressed the attack hard, and took still more heads.

sentences.zh: 眾方賀，芳遽策馬曰：「賊至矣。

translations.literal: The men were just congratulating when Fang suddenly spurred his horse and said, "The bandits have arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The men were still exchanging congratulations when Fang suddenly spurred his horse and cried, "The enemy is upon us!

sentences.zh: 」趣守險，而身斷後。

translations.literal: " He urged them to hold the defiles and personally brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged them to take the high ground and personally covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，寇果麕至。

translations.literal: Before long, the bandits indeed came swarming like deer in a herd.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the raiders came swarming in as Fang had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 芳戰益力，寇乃去。

translations.literal: Fang fought with increasing vigor, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fought all the harder, and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亡何，戰泥河，復大破之。

translations.literal: Before long, at Nihe he fought again and inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he fought them again at Nihe River and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 累遷指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he reached assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 以功，進都指揮僉事，充宣府遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and appointed roaming commander of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and appointed roaming commander of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 復以功，超遷都督僉事，隸總督為參將。

translations.literal: Again for merit he was skip-promoted to assistant commander-in-chief, serving under the governor-general as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Again for merit he was jump-promoted to assistant commander-in-chief and served under the governor-general as an assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 戰鎮山墩不利，奪俸。

translations.literal: At Zhenshandun the battle went badly and his salary was forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: A battle at Zhenshan Stockade went badly, and his salary was forfeited.

sentences.zh: 已，襲寇有功，進二秩，為右都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, in a raid on the bandits he had merit, advanced two ranks, and became right commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, in a successful raid on the enemy he was promoted two ranks and made right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋以功進左，賜蟒袍。

translations.literal: Soon for merit he was promoted to left and granted a python robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to left commander-in-chief for further merit and granted a python robe.

sentences.zh: 偏裨加左都督，自芳始也。

translations.literal: For a subordinate general to be raised to left commander-in-chief began with Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The precedent of elevating a subordinate officer to left commander-in-chief began with Fang.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，遷薊鎮副總兵，分守建昌。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to deputy supreme commander of the Jizhou garrison, separately guarding Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was made deputy supreme commander of the Jizhou garrison and posted to guard Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 土蠻十萬騎薄界嶺口，芳與總兵官歐陽安斬首數十，獲驍騎猛克兔等六人。

translations.literal: Tuman with one hundred thousand horsemen pressed close to Jieling Pass; Fang together with supreme commander Ouyang An beheaded several tens and captured six, including the fierce horseman Mengketu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Tuman approached Jieling Pass with one hundred thousand horsemen; Fang and Supreme Commander Ouyang An took several dozen heads and captured six men, including the crack rider Mengketu.

sentences.zh: 寇不知芳在，芳免胄示之，驚曰：「馬太師也！

translations.literal: The bandits did not know Fang was present; Fang removed his helmet to show himself, and they exclaimed in alarm, "It is Grand Mentor Ma!
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did not know Fang was there; he removed his helmet to reveal himself, and they cried in alarm, "It is Grand Mentor Ma!

sentences.zh: 」遂卻。

translations.literal: " Then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " At that they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，蔭世總旗。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, hereditary chief banner officer was conferred on his line.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the court, hereditary chief banner officer was conferred on his line.

sentences.zh: 未幾，辛愛、把都兒大入，躪遵化、玉田。

translations.literal: Before long, Xin Ai and Batu invaded on a large scale, trampling Zunhua and Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xin Ai and Batu launched a major invasion, ravaging Zunhua and Yutian.

sentences.zh: 芳追戰金山寺有功，而州縣破殘多，總督王忬以下俱獲罪，芳亦貶都督僉事。

translations.literal: Fang fought in pursuit at Jinshan Temple with merit, but many prefectures and counties were greatly devastated; Governor-General Wang Yu and all below were punished, and Fang was also demoted to assistant commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fang won merit pursuing the enemy at Jinshan Temple, but many prefectures and counties lay in ruins; Governor-General Wang Yu and his subordinates were all punished, and Fang was demoted to assistant commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋移守宣府。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 寇大入山西，芳一日夜馳五百里及之，七戰皆捷。

translations.literal: The bandits invaded Shanxi on a large scale; Fang in one day and night galloped five hundred li and caught up with them; seven battles were all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders plunged deep into Shanxi, Fang rode five hundred li in a day and a night to overtake them and won seven victories in succession.

sentences.zh: 已，復為左都督，就擢總兵官，以功進二秩。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again made left commander-in-chief, promptly promoted to supreme commander, and for merit advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to left commander-in-chief, immediately promoted to supreme commander, and advanced two more ranks for merit.

sentences.zh: 寇薄通州，芳入衛，令專護京師。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed close to Tongzhou; Fang entered in defense and was ordered to protect the capital exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders drew near Tongzhou, Fang rushed to the capital's defense and was ordered to guard the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 寇退，再進一秩。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, he was again promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew he was promoted one rank further.

sentences.zh: 尋與故總兵劉漢出北沙灘，搗寇巢。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to Beishatan with the former supreme commander Liu Han and struck at the bandits' nests.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined former Supreme Commander Liu Han in a raid from Beishatan against the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 已，坐寇入，令戴罪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because bandits had entered, he was ordered to serve with crimes pending.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made to serve while bearing the guilt of having allowed the enemy in.

sentences.zh: 四十五年七月，辛愛以十萬騎入西路，芳迎之馬蓮堡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the forty-fifth year, Xin Ai with one hundred thousand horsemen entered by the western route; Fang went to meet him at Malian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the forty-fifth year Xin Ai entered by the western route with one hundred thousand horsemen, and Fang went out to meet him at Malian Fort.

sentences.zh: 堡圮，眾請塞之，不可。

translations.literal: The fort walls had collapsed; the men asked to block them up, but he would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The fort walls had collapsed; his men urged him to seal them up, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 請登臺，亦不可。

translations.literal: They asked him to mount the tower, and that too he would not allow.
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to take the watchtower, and he refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 開堡四門，偃旗鼓，寂若無人。

translations.literal: He opened the fort's four gates, lowered banners and drums, and all was silent as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: He opened all four gates of the fort, lowered banners and stilled drums, and left the place silent as if deserted.

sentences.zh: 比暮，野燒燭天，囂呼達旦。

translations.literal: By evening, fires in the open country lit the sky; shouting and clamor lasted until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: By evening campfires blazed across the plain and the enemy's shouts carried until dawn.

sentences.zh: 芳臥，日中不起，敵騎窺者相屬，莫測所為。

translations.literal: Fang lay abed and did not rise even at midday; enemy horsemen came one after another to spy, unable to fathom what he was doing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang stayed in bed and did not rise even at midday, while enemy scouts came one after another, unable to guess his intent.

sentences.zh: 明日，芳蹶然起，乘城，指示眾曰：「彼軍多反顧，且走。

translations.literal: The next day Fang suddenly sprang up, mounted the wall, and pointed, telling the men, "Their army keeps looking back; they are about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fang sprang up at once, mounted the wall, and told his men, "Their army keeps glancing back—they are about to run.

sentences.zh: 」勒兵追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: " He drew up the troops in pursuit and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew up his troops in pursuit and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，或為辛愛謀，以五萬騎犯蔚州，誘芳出，而以五萬騎襲宣府城，可得誌。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, someone plotted for Xin Ai: with fifty thousand horsemen to invade Weizhou and lure Fang out, while with another fifty thousand horsemen to surprise Xuanfu city, thereby achieving their aim.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, a plan was made for Xin Ai: one force of fifty thousand horsemen would strike Weizhou to draw Fang out, while another fifty thousand would surprise Xuanfu and thus achieve their aim.

sentences.zh: 芳豫伐木環城，寇至不可上，遂解去。

translations.literal: Fang beforehand had timber felled to ring the city; when the bandits came they could not ascend, and so they dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had already had trees felled around the city walls; when the raiders arrived they could not scale them, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 頃之，率參將劉潭等出獨石塞外二百里，襲其帳於長水海。

translations.literal: Before long he led Assistant Commander Liu Tan and others two hundred li beyond Dushi Pass and raided their encampment at Changshuihai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he led Assistant Commander Liu Tan and others two hundred li beyond Dushi Pass and struck their camp at Changshuihai.

sentences.zh: 還至塞，追者及鞍子山。

translations.literal: Returning to the pass, pursuers caught up at Anzi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to the pass, pursuers caught up with him at Anzi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 迎戰，又大敗之。

translations.literal: He met them in battle and again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to fight and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 蔭子千戶。

translations.literal: His son was ennobled as thousand-household commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son was granted hereditary ennoblement as a thousand-household commandant.

sentences.zh: 芳有膽智，諳敵情，所至先士卒。

translations.literal: Fang had courage and wit, was thoroughly versed in the enemy's dispositions, and wherever he went placed himself before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was bold and shrewd, deeply versed in the enemy's ways, and always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 一歲數出師搗巢，或躬督戰，或遣裨將。

translations.literal: In one year he several times led forces out to strike at nests, sometimes personally supervising battle, sometimes dispatching subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Several times in a single year he led raids against enemy camps, sometimes commanding in person and sometimes sending subordinate generals.

sentences.zh: 家蓄健兒，得其死力。

translations.literal: At home he kept stalwart men and secured their utmost effort even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He kept stalwart fighters in his household and won their utter devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗命三十人出塞四百里，多所斬獲，寇大震。

translations.literal: Once he ordered thirty men to go four hundred li beyond the border; they killed and captured in great numbers, and the bandits were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent thirty men four hundred li beyond the border; they killed and captured in large numbers and the enemy was deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 芳乃帥師至大松林，頓舊興和衛，登高四望，耀兵而還。

translations.literal: Fang then led the army to Dasonglin, encamped at the old Xinghe Guard post, climbed high and looked in all four directions, displayed his might, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then marched his army to Great Pine Forest, camped at the old site of Xinghe Guard, climbed a height to survey the land in all directions, displayed his strength, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時大同被寇，視宣府尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time Datong suffered from bandits, even more severely than Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Datong was under heavy attack at the time, even more so than Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 總督陳其學恐擾畿輔，令總兵官趙岢扼紫荊關。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chen Qixue feared disturbance of the capital region and ordered Supreme Commander Zhao E to hold Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Chen Qixue, fearing raids on the capital region, ordered Supreme Commander Zhao E to hold Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 寇乃縱掠懷仁、山陰間，岢坐貶三秩，遂調芳與易鎮。

translations.literal: The bandits then ranged freely in plunder between Huairen and Shanyin; for this Zhao E was demoted three ranks, and Fang was transferred to exchange garrison commands with him.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders then ranged freely between Huairen and Shanyin; Zhao E was demoted three ranks for it, and Fang was transferred to swap garrison commands with him.

sentences.zh: 俺答轉犯威遠幾破，會其學率胡鎮等救，而芳軍亦至，相拒十余日，乃走。

translations.literal: Altan turned to attack Weiyuan and nearly took it; Chen Qixue happened to lead Hu Zhen and others to the rescue, and Fang's army also arrived; they held each other at bay for more than ten days, and Altan then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Altan turned on Weiyuan and nearly broke through, but Chen Qixue led Hu Zhen and others to the rescue and Fang's army also arrived; after more than ten days of stalemate Altan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 芳謂諸將曰：「大同非宣府比，與我間一墻耳。

translations.literal: Fang told the generals, "Datong is not to be compared with Xuanfu; it is separated from me by only one wall.
translations.idiomatic: Fang told his generals, "Datong is not like Xuanfu—it is only a wall away from us.

sentences.zh: 寇不時至，非大創之不可。

translations.literal: The bandits come at untimely intervals; unless they are grievously wounded it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: They raid without warning, and nothing less than a crushing blow will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」乃將兵出右衛，戰威寧海子，破之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led troops out from Right Guard, fought at Weininghaizi, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his troops out from Right Guard, fought at Weining Lake, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 其年，俺答就撫，塞上遂無事。

translations.literal: That year Altan submitted to pacification, and the border then had no disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: That year Altan accepted pacification, and the frontier was finally at peace.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，閱視侍郎吳百朋發芳行賄事，勒閑住。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, inspection vice minister Wu Baipeng exposed Fang's practice of bribery and ordered him to reside in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli, inspection vice minister Wu Baipeng exposed Fang's bribery and ordered him to stand down.

sentences.zh: 已，起僉書前軍都督府。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled to sign documents in the Front Army Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as signing officer of the Front Army Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 順義王要賞，聲言渝盟，復用芳鎮宣府。

translations.literal: The Shunyi Prince demanded rewards and declared the alliance violated; Fang was again employed to garrison Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunyi Prince demanded rewards and threatened to break the alliance, Fang was again posted to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 七年以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he requested retirement on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 芳起行伍，十余年為大帥。

translations.literal: Fang rose from the ranks; in little more than ten years he became a great commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rose from the ranks and in little more than ten years became a commanding general.

sentences.zh: 戰膳房堡、朔州、登鷹巢、鴿子堂、龍門、萬全右衛、東嶺、孤山、土木、乾莊、岔道、張家堡、得勝堡、大沙灘，大小百十接，身被數十創，以少擊眾，未嘗不大捷。

translations.literal: He fought at Shanfang Fort, Shuozhou, Dengyingchao, Gezitang, Longmen, Wanquan Right Guard, Dongling, Gushan, Tumu, Ganzhuang, Chadoo, Zhangjia Fort, Desheng Fort, and Dashatan — in all some one hundred and ten engagements large and small; his body bore several tens of wounds; with few he struck many, and never without great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Shanfang Fort, Shuozhou, Dengyingchao, Gezitang, Longmen, Wanquan Right Guard, Dongling, Gushan, Tumu, Ganzhuang, Chadoo, Zhangjia Fort, Desheng Fort, and Dashatan — some one hundred and ten engagements in all, large and small. His body bore dozens of wounds; fighting always against superior numbers, he never failed to win a major victory.

sentences.zh: 擒部長數十人，斬馘無算，威名震邊陲，為一時將帥冠。

translations.literal: He captured several tens of tribal chiefs; heads cut and ears taken were beyond counting; his martial renown shook the border regions, and he was the foremost of the generals of his day.
translations.idiomatic: He captured dozens of tribal chiefs and killed beyond count; his name shook the frontier, and he stood at the head of the commanders of his age.

sentences.zh: 石州城陷，副將田世威、參將劉寶論死，芳乞寢己蔭子，贖二將罪，為御史所劾，敕戒諭。

translations.literal: When Shizhou city fell, Vice Commander Tian Shiwei and Assistant Commander Liu Bao were sentenced to death; Fang begged to suspend the hereditary ennoblement of his own son to redeem the two generals' guilt, was impeached by a censor, and received an imperial admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhou fell, Vice Commander Tian Shiwei and Assistant Commander Liu Bao were condemned to death; Fang asked to forgo his own son's hereditary ennoblement to redeem them, was impeached by a censor, and received an imperial reprimand.

sentences.zh: 後世威復為將，遇芳薄，芳不與校，識者多之。

translations.literal: Later Shiwei again became a general; meeting Fang he treated him coldly, but Fang did not contend with him; the discerning praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shiwei returned to command; when he treated Fang coldly, Fang did not quarrel with him, and men of judgment admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 二子，棟、林。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Dong and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Dong and Lin.

sentences.zh: 棟官至都督，無所見。

translations.literal: Dong reached the rank of regional commander; nothing noteworthy is recorded of him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong rose to regional commander, but nothing noteworthy is recorded of him.

sentences.zh: 林，由父蔭累官大同參將。

translations.literal: Lin, through his father's hereditary privilege, cumulatively reached assistant commander of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, through his father's hereditary privilege, rose to assistant commander of Datong.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年，順義王撦力克縶獻史、車二部長，林以制敵功，進副總兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli, the Shunyi Prince Chelik bound and presented the chiefs of the Shi and Che tribes; Lin for merit in controlling the enemy was promoted to deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Wanli the Shunyi Prince Chelik bound and presented the chiefs of the Shi and Che tribes; for his success in checking the enemy Lin was promoted to deputy supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 二十七年擢署都督僉事，為遼東總兵官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and became supreme commander of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and appointed supreme commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 林雅好文學，能詩，工書，交遊多名士，時譽籍甚，自許亦甚高。

translations.literal: Lin by nature loved literature, could compose poetry, was skilled at calligraphy, associated with many famous scholars, was widely praised in his day, and thought highly of himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: Lin cultivated literature, wrote poetry, and was skilled at calligraphy; he moved among famous scholars, enjoyed wide acclaim, and held himself in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 嘗陳邊務十策，語多觸文吏，寢不行。

translations.literal: Once he submitted ten policies on frontier affairs; his words largely offended civil officials, and the matter was shelved without implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted ten proposals on frontier affairs, but his words offended many civil officials and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 稅使高淮橫恣，林力與抗。

translations.literal: Tax commissioner Gao Huai was overbearing and wanton; Lin forcefully resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Gao Huai ruled with arrogant cruelty, and Lin resisted him forcefully.

sentences.zh: 淮劾奏之，坐奪職。

translations.literal: Huai impeached and memorialized against him; for this Lin was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huai impeached him, and Lin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 給事中侯先春論救，改林戍煙瘴，先春亦左遷二官。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun argued in his defense; Lin's punishment was changed to garrison duty in miasmic lands, and Xianchun was also demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hou Xianchun pleaded his case; Lin's sentence was changed to service in the malarial south, and Hou Xianchun was also demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 久之，遇赦免。

translations.literal: After a long time he encountered an amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was pardoned in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 遼左用兵，詔林以故官從征。

translations.literal: When Liaodong raised arms, Lin was ordered by edict to follow the campaign with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Liaodong, an edict recalled Lin to campaign with his former rank.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬之四路出師也，令林將一軍由開原出三岔口，而以遊擊竇永澄監北關軍並進。

translations.literal: When Yang Hao sent out four routes, Lin was ordered to command one army from Kaiyuan through Sanchakou, while roaming commander Dou Yongcheng supervised the Beiguan army advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hao launched his four-route expedition, Lin was ordered to lead one army from Kaiyuan through Three Fork Pass, while Roaming Commander Dou Yongcheng supervised the Beiguan force advancing alongside him.

sentences.zh: 林軍至尚間崖結營浚壕，嚴斥堠自衛。

translations.literal: Lin's army reached Shangjian Cliff, encamped, dug moats, and strictly maintained outposts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army reached Shangjian Cliff, made camp, dug trenches, and posted scouts with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 及聞杜松軍敗，方移營，而大清兵已逼。

translations.literal: When he heard that Du Song's army had been defeated, he was just then moving camp when the Great Qing forces were already pressing close.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Du Song's army had been destroyed, Lin was moving camp just as Great Qing forces were already upon him.

sentences.zh: 乃還兵，別立營，浚壕三周，列火器壕外，更布騎兵於火器外，他士卒皆下馬，結方陣壕內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew back his troops, established a separate camp, dug moats on three sides, lined firearms outside the moats, further deployed cavalry outside the firearms, and all other soldiers dismounted and formed square battle formations inside the moats.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled his troops back, pitched a new camp, dug trenches on three sides, placed firearms beyond the trenches, posted cavalry beyond the firearms, and had the remaining infantry dismount and form square formations inside the trenches.

sentences.zh: 又一軍西營飛芬山。

translations.literal: Another army encamped to the west at Feifen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Another force encamped to the west at Feifen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 杜松軍既覆，大清兵乘銳薄林軍。

translations.literal: Du Song's army having been destroyed, the Great Qing forces, riding their sharp advantage, pressed close to Lin's army.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Song's army destroyed, the Great Qing forces, buoyed by victory, closed on Lin's army.

sentences.zh: 見林壕內軍已與壕外合而陳，縱精騎直前沖之。

translations.literal: Seeing that Lin's troops inside the moat had already joined those outside in battle formation, they released crack cavalry to charge straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Lin's men inside and outside the trenches already combined in battle order, they sent elite cavalry charging straight at them.

sentences.zh: 林軍不能支，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Lin's army could not hold and was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army could not hold and was routed.

sentences.zh: 副將麻巖戰死，林僅以數騎免。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Ma Yan died in battle; Lin escaped with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Ma Yan was killed in the fighting, and Lin escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 死者彌山谷，血流尚間崖下，水為之赤。

translations.literal: The dead filled the valleys; blood flowed below Shangjian Cliff, and the water turned red.
translations.idiomatic: The dead filled the valleys; blood ran below Shangjian Cliff until the water turned red.

sentences.zh: 大清遂移兵擊飛芬山。

translations.literal: The Great Qing forces then shifted troops to attack Feifen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing forces then turned to attack Feifen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 僉事潘宗顏等一軍亦覆。

translations.literal: The army of Assistant Commissioner Pan Zongyan and others was also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The force under Assistant Commissioner Pan Zongyan was also destroyed.

sentences.zh: 北關兵聞之，遂不敢進。

translations.literal: The Beiguan troops, hearing this, then dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Beiguan army heard the news, it dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 林既喪師，謫充為事官，俾守開原。

translations.literal: Lin having lost his army, was demoted to serving officer on probation and ordered to guard Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After losing his army Lin was demoted to probationary service officer and ordered to hold Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時蒙古宰賽、煖兔許助林兵，林與結約，恃此不設備。

translations.literal: At the time the Mongols Zaisai and Nuantu promised to aid Lin with troops; Lin made a pact with them and, relying on this, made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol leaders Zaisai and Nuantu had promised to aid Lin, and trusting that alliance he made no special preparations.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，大清兵忽臨城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, Great Qing forces suddenly arrived before the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year Great Qing forces suddenly appeared before the city.

sentences.zh: 林列眾城外，分少兵登陴。

translations.literal: Lin drew up his forces outside the city and assigned a small number of troops to mount the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: Lin drew up his army outside the walls and posted only a small guard on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 大清兵設盾梯進攻，而別以精騎擊破林軍之營東門外者。

translations.literal: The Great Qing forces deployed shield-ladders and advanced in attack, while separately with crack cavalry they broke the part of Lin's army encamped outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qing troops advanced with shielded ladders while a separate force of elite cavalry broke Lin's camp outside the east gate.

sentences.zh: 軍士爭門入，遂乘勢奪門，攻城兵亦逾城入。

translations.literal: The soldiers struggled to enter through the gate; the enemy then seized the momentum and took the gate, and the troops assaulting the city also scaled the walls and entered.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers scrambled through the gate to get inside; the enemy seized the gate in the confusion, and assault troops scaled the walls as well.

sentences.zh: 林城外軍望見盡奔。

translations.literal: Lin's army outside the city, seeing this, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's troops outside the walls saw what was happening and fled.

sentences.zh: 大清兵據城邀擊，壕不得渡，悉殲之。

translations.literal: The Great Qing forces held the city and intercepted them in attack; unable to cross the moat, all were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qing forces held the walls and cut them down at the moat; unable to cross, they were slaughtered to the last man.

sentences.zh: 林及副將於化龍、參將高貞、遊擊於守誌、守備何懋官等，皆死焉。

translations.literal: Lin together with Vice Commander Yu Hualong, Assistant Commander Gao Zhen, Roaming Commander Yu Shouzhi, Garrison Commander He Maoguan, and others all died there.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, Vice Commander Yu Hualong, Assistant Commander Gao Zhen, Roaming Commander Yu Shouzhi, Garrison Commander He Maoguan, and others all perished.

sentences.zh: 尋贈都督同知，進世蔭二秩。

translations.literal: Soon he was posthumously granted commander-in-chief and his line's hereditary privilege was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously granted the rank of commander-in-chief and his family's hereditary privilege was advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 林雖更歷邊鎮，然未經強敵，無大將才。

translations.literal: Although Lin had served in succession at border garrisons, he had never faced a powerful enemy and lacked the talent of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had served on several frontier postings, but he had never faced a truly formidable enemy and lacked the gifts of a great commander.

sentences.zh: 當事以虛名用之，故敗。

translations.literal: Those in charge employed him for empty reputation, and so he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him for his hollow reputation, and that is why he failed.

sentences.zh: 林五子，燃、熠、炯、爌，飈。

translations.literal: Lin had five sons: Ran, Yi, Jiong, Kuang, and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had five sons—Ran, Yi, Jiong, Kuang, and Biao.

sentences.zh: 燃、熠，戰死尚間崖。

translations.literal: Ran and Yi died in battle at Shangjian Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Ran and Yi were killed in battle at Shangjian Cliff.

sentences.zh: 炯，天啟中湖廣總兵官。

translations.literal: Jiong, during the Tianqi reign, was regional commander-in-chief of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong served as regional commander-in-chief of Huguang during the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 協討貴州叛賊，從王三善至大方，數戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He jointly campaigned against Guizhou rebels, followed Wang Sanshan to Dafang, and won victory in battle after battle.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Guizhou rebels, followed Wang Sanshan to Dafang, and won a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 已，大敗，三善自殺。

translations.literal: Soon after, they suffered a great defeat, and Sanshan killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they suffered a crushing defeat, and Sanshan took his own life.

sentences.zh: 炯潰歸。

translations.literal: Jiong fled in rout and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong broke and fled home.

sentences.zh: 得疾而卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 爌幼習兵略，天啟中為遼東遊擊。

translations.literal: Kuang from youth studied military strategy; during the Tianqi reign he was roaming commander in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang had studied military strategy since boyhood, and during the Tianqi reign he served as roaming commander in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 督師閣部孫承宗以其父死王事，獎用之，命代王楹守中右所。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and supreme commander Sun Chengzong, because his father had died in service to the state, rewarded and employed him, ordering him to replace Wang Ying in guarding Zhongyousuo.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and supreme commander Sun Chengzong, honoring him because his father had died in the state's service, gave him preferment and ordered him to replace Wang Ying in defending Zhongyousuo.

sentences.zh: 及巡撫袁崇煥更營制，以故官掌前鋒左營。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan reorganized the battalion system, with his former rank he took charge of the Vanguard Left Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Yuan Chonghuan reorganized the garrison system, Kuang retained his former rank and took command of the Vanguard Left Battalion.

sentences.zh: 數有功，屢遷至副總兵，守徐州。

translations.literal: He won merit repeatedly, was promoted again and again to deputy commander-in-chief, and guarded Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories he rose through the ranks to deputy commander-in-chief and was posted to defend Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年正月，賊陷鳳陽，大掠而去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Chongzhen, bandits captured Fengyang, plundered on a great scale, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 8, rebels seized Fengyang, looted the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爌及守備駱舉率兵入，以恢復告，遂留戍其地。

translations.literal: Kuang and garrison commander Luo Ju led troops in, reported the recovery, and thereupon remained to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and Garrison Commander Luo Ju marched in, reported the city's recovery, and remained to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊擾河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, bandits harassed Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month rebels raided Henan.

sentences.zh: 總督朱大典命移駐潁、毫。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhu Dadian ordered him to move and garrison Ying and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhu Dadian ordered him to redeploy to Yingzhou and Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 事定，還徐州。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he returned to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed, he returned to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊犯桐城，爌赴救，破之羅唱河。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, bandits invaded Tongcheng; Kuang went to the rescue and defeated them at the Luochang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when rebels struck Tongcheng, Kuang rushed to its aid and routed them on the Luochang River.

sentences.zh: 尋以護陵功，增秩一級。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit in guarding the imperial tombs, he was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted one rank for his service in guarding the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 歸德、徐州間有地曰朱家廠，土寇據之，時出掠。

translations.literal: Between Guide and Xuzhou there was a place called Zhujia Factory; local bandits held it and from time to time came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Between Guide and Xuzhou lay a place called Zhujiachang, held by local bandits who raided the countryside from time to time.

sentences.zh: 爌剿滅之。

translations.literal: Kuang suppressed and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 賊犯固始，大典檄爌及遊擊張士儀等分戍霍兵西南，扼賊東下，賊遂走六安。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded Gushi, Dadian ordered Kuang and roaming commander Zhang Shiyi and others to divide forces and garrison southwest of Huozhou, blocking the bandits' eastward advance; the bandits then fled toward Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels invaded Gushi, Dadian ordered Kuang, Roaming Commander Zhang Shiyi, and others to divide their forces and hold the southwest of Huozhou, blocking the enemy's eastward drive; the rebels then fled toward Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 大典又移爌等駐壽州東，兼護二陵。

translations.literal: Dadian again moved Kuang and the others to garrison east of Shouzhou, concurrently guarding the two imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Dadian then redeployed Kuang and his men east of Shouzhou, charging them also with guarding the two imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 當是時，長、淮南北，專以陵寢為重。

translations.literal: At that time, north and south of the Yangtze and Huai, priority was given solely to the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, throughout the lands north and south of the Yangtze and Huai, the imperial mausoleums were the overriding concern.

sentences.zh: 爌馳驅數年，幸無失事。

translations.literal: Kuang galloped about for several years and, by good fortune, suffered no mishap.
translations.idiomatic: For years Kuang rode hard from post to post, and by good fortune nothing went wrong.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月擢總兵官，鎮守天津。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief and stationed to guard Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to commander-in-chief and posted to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 久之，移鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to command Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to command Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十五年督三協副將王世寵、王加春、魯胤昌等討破叛番，斬首七百余級，撫安三十八族而還。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he directed the three assistant deputy commanders Wang Shichong, Wang Jiachun, Lu Yinchang, and others to campaign against and defeat rebellious tribes, beheading more than seven hundred, pacifying thirty-eight clans, and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he led the three assistant deputy commanders Wang Shichong, Wang Jiachun, and Lu Yinchang against rebellious tribes, took more than seven hundred heads, pacified thirty-eight clans, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 其冬，督師孫傳庭檄召不至，疏劾之。

translations.literal: That winter, supreme commander Sun Chuan summoned him by dispatch but he did not come; Chuan memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Supreme Commander Sun Chuan summoned him by dispatch, but Kuang failed to appear, and Chuan impeached him in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝令察爌堪辦賊，許戴罪圖功，否即以賜劍從事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an investigation into whether Kuang was fit to deal with bandits, permitting him to bear guilt while striving for merit; otherwise he was to be dealt with by the granted sword.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry into whether Kuang was fit to fight the rebels, allowing him to redeem himself while bearing guilt—or else to be executed under the sword of authority.

sentences.zh: 及爌至軍，傳庭貸其罪。

translations.literal: When Kuang reached the army, Chuan pardoned his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang reached the army, Chuan pardoned his offense.

sentences.zh: 已，復以逗留淫掠被劾，帝仍令載罪自效。

translations.literal: Soon after, he was again impeached for lingering and licentious plunder; the emperor still ordered him to carry guilt and redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached again for dawdling and pillaging, yet the emperor still allowed him to serve on while bearing guilt until he proved himself.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，傳庭將出關。

translations.literal: The next autumn, Chuan was about to march out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Chuan prepared to lead his army out of the pass.

sentences.zh: 有傳賊自內鄉窺商、雒者，檄爌移商州扼其北犯。

translations.literal: There were reports that bandits from Neixiang were watching Shang and Luo; he dispatched Kuang to move to Shangzhou and block their northward invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that rebels from Neixiang were eyeing Shangzhou and Luoyang; Chuan ordered Kuang to Shangzhou to block their northward thrust.

sentences.zh: 已而傳庭師覆，爌遂還鎮。

translations.literal: Before long Chuan's army was destroyed; Kuang thereupon returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chuan's army was annihilated, and Kuang returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷延綏、寧夏，遂陷蘭州，渡河抵甘州還攻之。

translations.literal: Before long, bandits captured Yansui and Ningxia, then captured Lanzhou, crossed the river, reached Ganzhou, and turned back to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels took Yansui and Ningxia, then Lanzhou, crossed the river, reached Ganzhou, and turned back to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 爌與巡撫林日瑞竭力固守。

translations.literal: Kuang and Grand Coordinator Lin Rirui exerted all their strength in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and Grand Coordinator Lin Rirui defended the city with everything they had.

sentences.zh: 賊乘雪夜坎而登。

translations.literal: The bandits, taking advantage of a snowy night, dug through and climbed up.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels exploited a snowy night to undermine the wall and scale it.

sentences.zh: 士卒寒甚，不能戰，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The soldiers were bitterly cold and could not fight; the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were frozen stiff and could not fight; the city fell.

sentences.zh: 爌、日瑞及中軍哈維新、姚世儒皆死焉。

translations.literal: Kuang, Rirui, and the central army officers Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru all died there.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, Lin Rirui, and the central army officers Ha Weixin and Yao Shiru all perished.

sentences.zh: 弟飈為沔陽州同知，城陷，亦死之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Biao was assistant prefect of Mianyang Prefecture; when the city fell, he too died there.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Biao, assistant prefect of Mianyang Prefecture, also died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 爌父子兄弟並死國難。

translations.literal: Kuang, his father, and his brothers all died in the nation's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, his father, and his brothers all died in the nation's ruin.

sentences.zh: 何卿，成都衛人。

translations.literal: He Qing was a man of the Chengdu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He Qing was a native of the Chengdu Guard.

sentences.zh: 有誌操，習武事。

translations.literal: He had integrity of purpose and studied military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed integrity and trained in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正德中，嗣世職為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he inherited his hereditary post as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he inherited his family's hereditary post as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 以能，擢筠連守備。

translations.literal: For his ability he was promoted to garrison commander of Junlian.
translations.idiomatic: For his ability he was promoted to garrison commander of Junlian.

sentences.zh: 從巡撫盛應期擊斬叛賊謝文禮、文義。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi in attacking and beheading the rebel bandits Xie Wenli and Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi in attacking and killing the rebel leaders Xie Wenli and Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，論功，進署都指揮僉事，充左參將，協守松潘。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, his merit was assessed; he was advanced to acting regional assistant commander, appointed left assistant commander, and jointly guarded Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Qing's merit was recognized: he was promoted to acting regional assistant commander, made left assistant commander, and posted to help defend Songpan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，芒部土舍隴政、土婦支祿等叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign, the Mangbu native chieftain Long Zheng, the indigenous woman Zhi Lu, and others rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign the Mangbu native chieftain Long Zheng, the indigenous woman Zhi Lu, and others rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 卿討之，斬首二百余級，降其眾數百人。

translations.literal: Qing campaigned against them, beheading more than two hundred, and accepting the surrender of several hundred of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Qing suppressed them, taking more than two hundred heads and accepting the surrender of several hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 政奔烏撒，卿檄土官安寧擒以獻。

translations.literal: Zheng fled to Wusa; Qing dispatched orders to the native official Anning to capture and present him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng fled to Wusa, and Qing ordered the native official Anning to seize him and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 寧佯諾，而匿政不出。

translations.literal: Anning feigned agreement but hid Zheng and would not produce him.
translations.idiomatic: Anning pretended to comply but hid Zheng and refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 巡撫湯沐言狀，帝奪卿冠帶。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Tang Mu reported the situation; the emperor stripped Qing of his official insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Tang Mu reported what had happened, and the emperor stripped Qing of his rank and insignia.

sentences.zh: 川、貴兵合討，賊始滅，還冠帶如初。

translations.literal: Sichuan and Guizhou troops jointly campaigned; the bandits were finally destroyed, and his insignia were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan and Guizhou forces joined the campaign and the rebels were finally destroyed, his rank and insignia were restored.

sentences.zh: 五年春擢卿副總兵，仍鎮松潘。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Qing was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief and still commanded Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief and continued to command Songpan.

sentences.zh: 隴氏已絕，改芒部為鎮雄府，設流官。

translations.literal: The Long clan was extinct; Mangbu was changed to Zhenxiong Prefecture and regular appointed officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: With the Long clan extinct, Mangbu was reorganized as Zhenxiong Prefecture and placed under regular appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，政遺黨沙保復叛。

translations.literal: Before long, Zheng's remaining followers, Sha Bao, rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zheng's remnant follower Sha Bao rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 卿偕參將魏武、參議姚汝臯等並進，斬保等賊首七人，余盡殄。

translations.literal: Qing together with Assistant Commander Wei Wu, Administrative Assistant Yao Rugao, and others advanced together, beheading seven bandit chiefs including Bao; the rest were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Qing advanced with Assistant Commander Wei Wu, Administrative Assistant Yao Rugao, and others, beheaded seven rebel leaders including Sha Bao, and wiped out the rest.

sentences.zh: 錄功，武最，卿次之，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded: Wu ranked first, Qing second; rewards were granted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was recorded, Wu ranked first and Qing second; each received rewards according to his service.

sentences.zh: 黑虎五砦番反，圍長安諸堡，烏都、鵓鴿諸番亦繼叛。

translations.literal: The Black Tiger Five Stockades tribes rebelled and besieged the forts of Chang'an; the Wudu, Zhegu, and other tribes also rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of the Black Tiger Five Stockades rose up and besieged the Chang'an forts, and the Wudu, Zhegu, and other tribes followed in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 卿皆破平之，就進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Qing defeated and pacified them all, and was thereupon promoted to regional assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qing defeated and pacified them all and was promoted on the spot to regional assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 威茂番十余砦連兵劫軍餉，且攻茂州及長寧諸堡，要撫賞。

translations.literal: More than ten stockades of Weimao tribes joined forces to plunder military provisions, and moreover attacked Maozhou and the forts of Changning, demanding pacification rewards.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten Weimao stockades joined forces to raid military supplies and attack Maozhou and the Changning forts, demanding pacification payments.

sentences.zh: 卿與副使朱紈築茂州外城以困之。

translations.literal: Qing together with Vice Commissioner Zhu Wan built Maozhou's outer wall to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Vice Commissioner Zhu Wan built an outer wall around Maozhou to pin the tribes down.

sentences.zh: 旋以計殘其眾，戰屢捷，遂攻深溝，焚其碉砦。

translations.literal: Soon, by stratagem he wore down their forces; in battle he won victory repeatedly, then attacked Shengou and burned their blockhouses and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wore their forces down by stratagem, won battle after battle, stormed Shengou, and burned their blockhouses and stockades.

sentences.zh: 諸番窘，請贖罪。

translations.literal: The tribes, hard pressed, requested to redeem their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, the tribes begged to atone for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 卿責獻首惡，番不應。

translations.literal: Qing demanded they hand over the chief culprits; the tribes did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Qing demanded the ringleaders, but the tribes refused.

sentences.zh: 復分剿淺溝、渾水二砦殲之。

translations.literal: He again divided forces to suppress and destroy the two stockades of Qiangou and Hunshui.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his forces, stormed the Qiangou and Hunshui stockades, and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 諸番乃爭獻首惡，插血斷指耳，誓不復叛。

translations.literal: The tribes then vied to present the chief culprits, inserting blood, severing fingers and ears, and swearing never again to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then competed to surrender the ringleaders, swearing blood oaths by pricking their flesh, severing fingers and ears, and vowing never to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 卿乃與刻木為約，分處其曹，畫疆守，松潘路復通。

translations.literal: Qing then made a carved-wood covenant with them, divided and settled their groups, demarcated boundaries for guarding, and the Songpan route was restored to passage.
translations.idiomatic: Qing then carved a wooden covenant with them, resettled their clans under fixed boundaries, and the road to Songpan was open once more.

sentences.zh: 巡撫潘鑒等上二人功，詔賚銀幣，進署都督同知，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Pan Jian and others submitted the merit of the two men; an edict granted silver and silks, and Qing was advanced to acting regional vice commander while his garrison command remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Pan Jian and others reported the achievements of the two men; an edict granted silver and silks, and Qing was promoted to acting regional vice commander while remaining in command.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time, on grounds of illness he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，塞上多警。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, there were many alarms on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the frontier was rife with alarms.

sentences.zh: 召卿，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Qing was summoned; he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was summoned, but he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪其都督，命以都指揮使詣部聽調。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped him of his regional commander rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry as regional commander to await assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, stripped him of his regional commander's rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry as a regional commander awaiting assignment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寇逼畿輔，命營盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Before long, invaders pressed close to the capital region; he was ordered to encamp at Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when raiders threatened the capital region, he was ordered to encamp at Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 松潘副總兵李爵為巡撫丘養浩劾罷，詔以卿代。

translations.literal: Songpan deputy commander-in-chief Li Jue was impeached and dismissed by Grand Coordinator Qiu Yanghao; an edict ordered Qing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Songpan Deputy Commander Li Jue was impeached and dismissed by Grand Coordinator Qiu Yanghao, an edict appointed Qing in his place.

sentences.zh: 給事中許天倫言卿賄養浩劾爵，自為地。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Tianlun said Qing had bribed Yanghao to impeach Jue, clearing space for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Tianlun charged that Qing had bribed Qiu Yanghao to impeach Li Jue and clear the way for himself.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，褫卿及養浩官，令巡按冉崇禮核實。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped Qing and Yanghao of office, and ordered Investigating Censor Ran Chongli to verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, stripped both Qing and Yanghao of office, and ordered Investigating Censor Ran Chongli to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時兵事棘，翁萬達復薦卿，還其都督僉事，都東官廳軍馬。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs were urgent; Weng Wanda again recommended Qing, restored his regional assistant commander rank, and put him in command of the Eastern Office's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: With military affairs critical, Weng Wanda recommended Qing again; his rank as regional assistant commander was restored and he was put in command of the Eastern Office forces.

sentences.zh: 已而崇禮具言爵貪汙，「卿鎮松潘十七年，為蜀保障，軍民頌德，且貧，安所得賄？

translations.literal: Later Chongli reported fully that Jue was corrupt: "Qing has guarded Songpan for seventeen years, serving as Sichuan's bulwark; soldiers and civilians praise his virtue, and moreover he is poor—whence would he obtain bribes?
translations.idiomatic: Later Ran Chongli reported in full that Li Jue was corrupt: "Qing has held Songpan for seventeen years as Sichuan's shield; soldiers and civilians praise his virtue, and he is poor besides—where would he find the money for a bribe?

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃解。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 四川白草番為亂，副總兵高岡鳳被劾。

translations.literal: The Baicao tribes of Sichuan rose in disorder; deputy commander-in-chief Gao Gangfeng was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: When the Baicao tribes of Sichuan rebelled, Deputy Commander Gao Gangfeng was impeached.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書路迎奏卿代之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Lu Ying memorialized that Qing should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Lu Ying recommended Qing to replace him.

sentences.zh: 卿再蒞松潘，將士鹹喜。

translations.literal: Qing again arrived at Songpan; officers and soldiers all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing returned to Songpan, officers and soldiers alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 乃會巡撫張時徹討擒渠惡數人，俘斬九百七十有奇，克營砦四十七，毀碉房四千八百，獲馬牛器械儲積各萬計。

translations.literal: He then joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Shiche in campaigning against and capturing several ringleaders, taking prisoners and beheading more than nine hundred seventy, capturing forty-seven camps and stockades, destroying four thousand eight hundred blockhouses, and seizing horses, cattle, weapons, and stored provisions each numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Shiche in hunting down several ringleaders, killing and capturing more than nine hundred seventy of the enemy, taking forty-seven camps and stockades, destroying four thousand eight hundred blockhouses, and seizing horses, cattle, weapons, and stores by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting regional vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 卿素有威望，為番人所憚。

translations.literal: Qing had long possessed prestige and was feared by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had long commanded respect, and the tribes feared him.

sentences.zh: 自威茂迄松潘、龍安夾道築墻數百里，行旌往來，無剽奪患。

translations.literal: From Weimao through Songpan and Long'an, walls were built for several hundred li along the route; official banners came and went without the trouble of plunder.
translations.idiomatic: From Weimao through Songpan and Long'an he had walls built for hundreds of li along the road, so that official processions could pass without fear of robbery.

sentences.zh: 先後蒞鎮二十四年，軍民戴之若慈母。

translations.literal: In all he held command for twenty-four years; soldiers and civilians cherished him as they would a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty-four years in command, soldiers and civilians revered him as they would a loving mother.

sentences.zh: 再以疾歸。

translations.literal: Again on grounds of illness he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired again on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，倭寇海上。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Japanese pirates raided the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year Japanese pirates raided the coast.

sentences.zh: 詔卿與沈希儀各率家眾赴蘇、松軍門。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qing and Shen Xiyi each to lead their household followers to the Suzhou-Songjiang military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qing and Shen Xiyi each to lead their household troops to the Suzhou-Songjiang military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 明年充副總兵，總理浙江及蘇、松海防。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed deputy commander-in-chief and put in overall charge of Zhejiang and the Suzhou-Songjiang coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made deputy commander-in-chief with overall charge of coastal defense in Zhejiang, Suzhou, and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 卿，蜀中名將，不諳海道，年已老，兵與將不習，竟不能有所為。

translations.literal: Qing was a famous general of Shu, unfamiliar with sea routes; he was already old, and troops and commander were unaccustomed to one another—ultimately he could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was a famed general of Shu, but he knew nothing of the sea; he was old, his men and he were strangers to one another, and in the end he achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 為巡按御史周如鬥劾罷，卒。

translations.literal: He was impeached and dismissed by Investigating Censor Zhou Rudou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zhou Rudou impeached him and had him removed from office; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 沈希儀，字唐佐，貴縣人。

translations.literal: Shen Xiyi, styled Tangzuo, was a man of Guixian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xiyi, styled Tangzuo, was a native of Guixian.

sentences.zh: 嗣世職為奉議衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He inherited his hereditary post as commander of the Fengyi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his family's hereditary post as commander of the Fengyi Guard.

sentences.zh: 機警有膽勇，智計過絕於人。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and possessed courage, and his stratagems surpassed those of ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and bold, he possessed a cunning that set him apart from other men.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年，調征永安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he was transferred to campaign in Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign he was transferred to campaign in Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 以數百人搗陳村砦，馬陷淖中，騰而上，連馘三酋，破其余眾。

translations.literal: With several hundred men he struck Chen Village Stockade; his horse sank in the mire, but he leapt up, severed three chieftains' heads in succession, and broke the rest of their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Leading several hundred men he stormed Chen Village Stockade; when his horse sank in the mud he sprang free, took three chieftains' heads in succession, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 進署都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting regional assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting regional assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 義寧賊寇臨桂，還巢，希儀追之。

translations.literal: Yining bandits raided Lin Gui, returned to their lair, and Xiyi pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits from Yining raided Lin Gui and withdrew to their lair; Xiyi pursued them.

sentences.zh: 巢有兩隘，賊伏兵其一，使熟瑤紿官兵入。

translations.literal: The lair had two passes; the bandits hid troops at one and had acculturated Yao deceive the government troops into entering.
translations.idiomatic: The lair had two passes. The bandits lay in wait at one and sent acculturated Yao to lure the government troops in.

sentences.zh: 希儀策其詐，急從別隘直抵賊巢。

translations.literal: Xiyi guessed their deception and hastily took the other pass straight to the bandits' lair.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing the ruse, Xiyi rushed by the other pass straight into the bandits' stronghold.

sentences.zh: 賊倉卒還救，遂大破之。

translations.literal: The bandits hurried back to rescue it and were thereupon routed on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rushed back to its defense and were utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 荔浦賊八千渡江東掠，希儀率五百人駐白面砦，待其歸。

translations.literal: Eight thousand Lipu bandits crossed the river to raid eastward; Xiyi led five hundred men to garrison White Face Stockade and waited for their return.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand Lipu bandits crossed the river to raid the east country. Xiyi took five hundred men to White Face Stockade and waited for their return.

sentences.zh: 砦去蛟龍、滑石兩灘各數里。

translations.literal: The stockade was several li from each of the two fords, Jiaolong and Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade stood several li from each of the Jiaolong and Huashi fords.

sentences.zh: 希儀以滑石灘狹，雖眾可薄，蛟龍灘廣，濟則難圖，欲誘致之滑石。

translations.literal: Xiyi considered that Huashi Ford was narrow and though they were many they could be pressed; Jiaolong Ford was broad—once they crossed it would be hard to attack; he wished to lure them to Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: Huashi Ford was narrow—even a large force could be pressed there—while Jiaolong Ford was wide and hard to attack once they had crossed. Xiyi meant to lure them to Huashi.

sentences.zh: 乃樹旗百蛟龍灘，守以羸卒，然柴以疑之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised a hundred banners at Jiaolong Ford, garrisoned it with weak troops, and lit fires to make them suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He planted a hundred banners at Jiaolong Ford, left a weak garrison, and lit bonfires to feign strength.

sentences.zh: 賊果趨滑石。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed rushed toward Huashi.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did as he hoped and headed for Huashi.

sentences.zh: 希儀預以小艦載勁卒伏葭葦中。

translations.literal: Xiyi beforehand had small boats carry picked troops hidden among the reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had already hidden picked men aboard small boats in the reeds.

sentences.zh: 賊渡且半，乘瀧急沖之，兩岸軍噪而前，賊眾多墜水死，收所掠而還。

translations.literal: When the bandits were half across, he took advantage of the swift current to strike them; troops on both banks shouted and advanced; many bandits fell into the water and died; he recovered what had been plundered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were half across, he drove into them on the swift current while troops on both banks shouted and closed in. Many drowned; he recovered the loot and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 從副總兵張祐連破臨桂、灌陽、古田賊。

translations.literal: Following Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhang You, he successively defeated the bandits of Lin Gui, Guanyang, and Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Deputy Commander Zhang You, he broke the bandits of Lin Gui, Guanyang, and Gutian in succession.

sentences.zh: 進署都指揮同知，掌都司事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting assistant commander-in-chief and put in charge of the regional military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting assistant commander-in-chief and given charge of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年，總督姚鏌將討田州岑猛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Yao Mo was about to campaign against Cen Meng of Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 5, Grand Coordinator Yao Mo prepared to campaign against Cen Meng of Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 用希儀計，間猛婦翁歸順土酋岑璋，使圖猛，而分兵五哨進。

translations.literal: Using Xiyi's plan, he estranged Meng's wife's father, Guishun native chieftain Cen Zhang, had him plot against Meng, and divided the army into five columns to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xiyi's plan, he drove a wedge between Meng and his father-in-law Cen Zhang, chieftain of Guishun, set Zhang to plot against Meng, and sent five columns forward.

sentences.zh: 希儀將中哨，當工堯。

translations.literal: Xiyi commanded the center column and faced Gongyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi led the center column against Gongyao.

sentences.zh: 工堯，賊要地，聚眾守之。

translations.literal: Gongyao was a strategic point for the bandits; they gathered a host to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyao was a key stronghold, defended by a mass of rebels.

sentences.zh: 希儀夜遣軍三百人，緣山上，繞出其背。

translations.literal: Xiyi by night sent three hundred troops to climb the mountain and circle behind them.
translations.idiomatic: By night Xiyi sent three hundred men up the mountain to get behind them.

sentences.zh: 比明合戰，則所遣軍已立幟山巔，賊大潰敗。

translations.literal: By dawn when battle joined, the troops he had sent already had banners planted on the mountaintop; the bandits fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, as battle was joined, his detachment already stood on the summit with banners flying, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 猛走歸順，為璋所執，田州平。

translations.literal: Meng fled to Guishun and was seized by Zhang; Tianzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Meng fled to Guishun, was seized by Zhang, and Tianzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 希儀功最，鏌抑之，止受賚。

translations.literal: Xiyi's merit was greatest, but Mo suppressed him; he received only an award of gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had done the most, but Yao Mo downplayed him and he received only an imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 鏌議設流官，希儀曰：「思恩以流官故，亂至今未已。

translations.literal: Mo proposed installing regular officials; Xiyi said: "Because Si'en had regular officials appointed, disorder has continued to the present and has not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Mo proposed installing regular officials. Xiyi said, "Si'en was given regular officials, and the unrest there has never ended.

sentences.zh: 田州復然，兩賊且合從起。

translations.literal: If Tianzhou is treated the same, the two bandit forces will ally and rise together."
translations.idiomatic: Do the same at Tianzhou, and the two rebel camps will join forces and rise together."

sentences.zh: 」鏌不從。

translations.literal: Mo did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Mo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 以希儀為右參將，分守思、田。

translations.literal: Xiyi was made Right Assistant Regional Commander, with divided duty guarding Si'en and Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was made right assistant regional commander with divided duty over Si'en and Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 希儀請還鄉治裝。

translations.literal: Xiyi requested leave to return home to pack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi asked leave to go home and pack.

sentences.zh: 以參將張經代守。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Zhang Jing was substituted to hold the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Regional Commander Zhang Jing was sent to hold the garrison in his place.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，田州復叛，鏌罷歸。

translations.literal: Barely a month later Tianzhou rebelled again and Mo was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later Tianzhou rebelled again; Mo was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 王守仁代，多用希儀計，思、田復定。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren replaced him, used many of Xiyi's plans, and Si'en and Tianzhou were pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren replaced him, relied heavily on Xiyi's plans, and Si'en and Tianzhou were pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 改右江柳慶參將，駐柳州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right River Liujing Assistant Regional Commander and stationed at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as right-river Liujing assistant regional commander and posted to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 象州、武宣、融縣瑤反，討破之。

translations.literal: The Yao of Xiangzhou, Wuxuan, and Rong County rebelled; he campaigned and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Xiangzhou, Wuxuan, and Rong County rebelled; he defeated them in campaign.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸，頃之還故任。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and went home; soon after he returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired; before long he was back in his old post.

sentences.zh: 柳在萬山中，城外五里即賊巢，軍民至無地可田，而官軍素罷不任戰。

translations.literal: Liuzhou lay among myriad mountains; five li outside the city walls were bandit lairs; soldiers and civilians had no land to farm, and government troops were by nature lax and unfit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzhou sat deep in the mountains; five li beyond the walls lay bandit lairs. Soldiers and civilians had nowhere to farm, and the regular troops were slack and unfit for war.

sentences.zh: 又賊耳目遍官府，閨闥動靜無不知。

translations.literal: Moreover the bandits had eyes and ears throughout the government offices; nothing that moved within women's chambers was unknown to them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits also had spies in every yamen; not a whisper in the inner quarters escaped them.

sentences.zh: 希儀謂欲大破賊，非狼兵不可，請於制府。

translations.literal: Xiyi said that to break the bandits on a large scale Lang troops were indispensable; he requested this of the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi said that only Lang troops could break the bandits for good and petitioned the governor-general.

sentences.zh: 調那地狼兵二千來，戍兵稍振。

translations.literal: Two thousand Nadi Lang troops were summoned; the garrison troops were somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand Nadi Lang troops were called up, and the garrison regained some fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 乃求得與瑤通販易者數十人，持其罪而厚撫之，使诇賊。

translations.literal: He then found several dozen men who traded with the Yao, held their crimes over them but treated them generously, and had them spy on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then found several dozen men who traded with the Yao, pardoned their crimes with generous rewards, and set them to spy on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊動靜，希儀亦無不知。

translations.literal: As to the bandits' movements, Xiyi likewise knew everything.
translations.idiomatic: In turn, Xiyi knew every move the bandits made.

sentences.zh: 希儀每出兵，雖肘腋親近不得聞。

translations.literal: Each time Xiyi took the field, even his closest attendants were not told.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiyi marched out, not even his closest aides were told beforehand.

sentences.zh: 至期鳴號，則諸軍鹹集。

translations.literal: When the time came he sounded the signal, and all the troops assembled.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour he sounded the muster, and every unit gathered.

sentences.zh: 令一人挾旗引諸軍行，不測所往。

translations.literal: He ordered one man carrying a banner to lead the troops; none could tell where they were going.
translations.idiomatic: One man with a banner led the columns, and no one knew where they were bound.

sentences.zh: 及駐軍設伏，賊必至，遇伏輒奔。

translations.literal: When he encamped and set ambushes, the bandits always came; meeting ambush they always fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he laid an ambush, the bandits walked into it—and always broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊之，無不如誌。

translations.literal: When government troops struck, nothing failed to go as planned.
translations.idiomatic: Every government strike landed exactly as he had planned.

sentences.zh: 已，賊寇他所，官軍又先至。

translations.literal: Afterward, when bandits raided some other place, government troops had already arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits struck elsewhere, government troops were already there.

sentences.zh: 遠村僻聚，賊度官軍所不逮者，往寇之，官軍又未嘗不在，賊驚以為神。

translations.literal: Remote villages and secluded settlements—the bandits judged government troops could not reach—would still find government troops there when they went to raid; the bandits marveled, thinking it supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: Even remote hamlets the bandits thought beyond government reach would find troops waiting when they came to raid. They took it for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 希儀得賊巢婦女畜產，果鄰巢者悉還之，惟取陰助賊者。

translations.literal: When Xiyi obtained women, livestock, and goods from bandit lairs, if they belonged to neighboring lairs he returned all of them, taking only those who had secretly aided the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When he seized women, livestock, and goods from a bandit lair, he returned everything that belonged to neighboring lairs and kept only those who had secretly helped the bandits.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤盡詟伏，無敢向賊。

translations.literal: All the Yao were thoroughly cowed and dared not turn toward the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao were thoroughly cowed and dared not side with the bandits.

sentences.zh: 希儀初至，令熟瑤得出入城中，無所禁。

translations.literal: When Xiyi first arrived, he allowed acculturated Yao free entry and exit in the city with no restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyi first arrived, he let acculturated Yao come and go in the city without restriction.

sentences.zh: 因厚賞其黠者，使為諜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he richly rewarded the clever ones and had them serve as spies.
translations.idiomatic: He richly rewarded the shrewdest among them and made them his spies.

sentences.zh: 後漸令瑤婦入見其妻，賚以酒食繒帛。

translations.literal: Later he gradually had Yao women come in to see his wife, bestowing wine, food, silk, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he had Yao women visit his wife, lavishing wine, food, silk, and cloth on them.

sentences.zh: 其夫常以賊情告者，則陰厚之。

translations.literal: Those whose husbands often reported bandit intelligence he secretly rewarded generously.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly rewarded the husbands of those who brought bandit intelligence.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤婦利賞，爭勸其夫輸賊情，或自入府言之。

translations.literal: Yao women coveted the rewards and vied to persuade their husbands to give intelligence on the bandits, or came themselves into the prefecture to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for the rewards, Yao women urged their husbands to inform on the bandits—or came to the yamen themselves.

sentences.zh: 以故，賊益無所匿形。

translations.literal: For this reason the bandits had ever less place to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the bandits had nowhere left to hide.

sentences.zh: 希儀每於風雨晦冥夜，偵賊所止宿，分遣人賫銃潛伏舍旁。

translations.literal: Xiyi often on nights of wind, rain, and murky darkness tracked where bandits lodged and sent men bearing muskets to lie hidden beside their houses.
translations.idiomatic: On stormy, pitch-dark nights Xiyi would track where bandits slept and send men with muskets to lie in wait beside their houses.

sentences.zh: 中夜銃舉，賊大駭曰：「老沈來矣！

translations.literal: At midnight muskets were fired; the bandits were greatly terrified and said: "Old Shen is here!
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the muskets fired. The bandits cried in terror, "Old Shen is here!

sentences.zh: 」鹹挈妻子匍匐上山。

translations.literal: " All grabbed wives and children and crawled up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone grabbed wife and child and crawled up the mountain.

sentences.zh: 兒啼女號，或寒凍觸厓石死，爭怨悔作賊非計。

translations.literal: Infants cried and women wailed; some died from cold striking cliff rocks; all complained and regretted that banditry was no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Babies wailed and women screamed; some froze against the cliffs and died. All cursed the life of banditry.

sentences.zh: 至曉下山，則寂無人聲。

translations.literal: At dawn when they descended the mountain, it was silent—no human voices.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they came down the mountain to find the valley empty and silent.

sentences.zh: 他巢亦然，眾愈益驚。

translations.literal: Other lairs were the same; the crowd grew ever more terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The same thing happened at every lair, and terror spread.

sentences.zh: 潛遣人入城偵之，則希儀故居城中不出也。

translations.literal: Secretly sending men into the city to spy, they found Xiyi had always been at home in the city and had not gone out.
translations.idiomatic: Spies sent secretly into the city found Xiyi had never left his residence.

sentences.zh: 賊膽落，多易面為熟瑤。

translations.literal: The bandits' courage collapsed; many changed appearance to become acculturated Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits' nerve broke; many disguised themselves as acculturated Yao.

sentences.zh: 韋扶諫者，馬平瑤魁也，累捕不得。

translations.literal: Wei Fujian was the Yao chieftain of Maping; repeated captures failed to get him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fujian, chieftain of the Maping Yao, had eluded capture again and again.

sentences.zh: 有報扶諫逃鄰賊三層巢者，希儀潛率兵剿之，則又與三層賊往劫他所。

translations.literal: Report came that Fujian had fled to the neighboring bandits' Three-layer Lair; Xiyi secretly led troops to exterminate it, but Fujian had again gone with the Three-layer bandits to raid elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Fujian had fled to the neighboring Three-layer Lair. Xiyi secretly led troops against it, only to find Fujian had gone raiding elsewhere with the Three-layer bandits.

sentences.zh: 希儀盡俘三層巢妻子歸，希儀俘賊妻子盡以畀狼兵，至是獨閉之空舍，飲食之。

translations.literal: Xiyi captured all the wives and children of Three-layer Lair and returned; Xiyi had always given captured bandits' wives and children to Lang troops—this time alone he shut them in empty houses and fed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi took all the wives and children of Three-layer Lair captive. He had always handed such captives to the Lang troops; this time he shut them in empty houses and fed them.

sentences.zh: 使熟瑤往語其夫曰：「得韋扶諫，還矣。

translations.literal: He had acculturated Yao go and tell their husbands: "Obtain Wei Fujian and they will be returned.
