translations.idiomatic: He sent acculturated Yao to tell the husbands, "Produce Wei Fujian and your families will be returned.

sentences.zh: 」諸瑤聞，悉來謁希儀。

translations.literal: " Hearing this, all the Yao came to pay court to Xiyi.
translations.idiomatic: " At the news, every Yao headman came before Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 今入室視之，妻子固無恙。

translations.literal: Now entering the rooms to look, their wives and children were indeed unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: They were shown their wives and children unharmed.

sentences.zh: 乃共誘扶諫出巢，縛以獻，易妻子還。

translations.literal: Together they lured Fujian out of the lair, bound him and presented him, and exchanged him for the return of their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Together they lured Fujian from his lair, bound him, and delivered him up in exchange for their families.

sentences.zh: 希儀剜扶諫目，支解之，懸諸城門。

translations.literal: Xiyi gouged out Fujian's eyes, dismembered him, and hung him at the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi gouged out Fujian's eyes, dismembered him, and hung the pieces at the city gates.

sentences.zh: 諸瑤服希儀威信，益不敢為盜。

translations.literal: All the Yao submitted to Xiyi's prestige and authority and dared less to become robbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao submitted to Xiyi's authority and scarcely dared rob again.

sentences.zh: 自是，柳城四旁數百里，無敢攘奪者。

translations.literal: From then on, for several hundred li around Liucheng, none dared seize by force.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, for hundreds of li around Liucheng, no one dared plunder.

sentences.zh: 希儀嘗上書於朝，言狼兵亦瑤、僮耳。

translations.literal: Xiyi once memorialized the court, saying Lang troops were also Yao and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi once memorialized the throne: the Lang troops were Yao and Zhuang too.

sentences.zh: 瑤、僮所在為賊，而狼兵死不敢為非，非狼兵順，而瑤、僮逆也。

translations.literal: Wherever Yao and Zhuang were, they became bandits, yet Lang troops to the death dared not do wrong—it was not that Lang troops were obedient while Yao and Zhuang were rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Where Yao and Zhuang served regular officials they turned bandit, yet Lang troops under native chiefs would not dare misbehave on pain of death. The difference was not nature but governance.

sentences.zh: 狼兵隸土官，瑤、僮隸流官。

translations.literal: Lang troops belonged to native officials; Yao and Zhuang belonged to regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lang troops answered to native officials; Yao and Zhuang answered to regular officials.

sentences.zh: 土官令嚴足以制狼兵，流官勢輕不能制瑤、僮。

translations.literal: Native officials' orders were strict enough to control Lang troops; regular officials' authority was light and could not control Yao and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs ruled with enough severity to command Lang troops; regular magistrates lacked the weight to control Yao and Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 若割瑤、僮分隸之旁近土官，土官世世富貴，不敢有他望。

translations.literal: If Yao and Zhuang were carved up and placed under nearby native officials, the native officials would be rich and noble generation after generation and would not dare cherish other hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Partition the Yao and Zhuang among nearby native chiefs, and those chiefs would grow rich and loyal for generations, with no ambition beyond their domains.

sentences.zh: 以國家之力制土官，以土官之力制瑤、僮，皆為狼兵，兩廣世世無患矣。

translations.literal: Use the state's power to control native officials, use native officials' power to control Yao and Zhuang—all would become Lang troops, and the Two Guangs would be free of trouble for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Let the state hold the native chiefs, let the native chiefs hold the Yao and Zhuang—all would fight as Lang troops do, and the Two Guangs would know peace for generations.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 至十六年而有思恩岑金之變。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year there was the Si'en Cen Jin disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year came the Si'en rebellion led by Cen Jin.

sentences.zh: 初，思恩土官岑浚既誅，改設流官，以其酋二人韋貴、徐五為土巡檢，分掌其兵各萬余。

translations.literal: Initially, after Si'en native official Cen Jun was executed, regular officials were installed, and two of his chieftains Wei Gui and Xu Wu were made native sub-inspectors, each commanding over ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the Si'en native official Cen Jun was executed, the post was given to regular magistrates and two of his chiefs, Wei Gui and Xu Wu, were made native sub-inspectors, each commanding more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 夷民不樂漢法，凡數叛。

translations.literal: The tribal people did not delight in Han law; they rebelled several times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen chafed under Han law and rebelled repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 鎮安有男子名金，自言浚子。

translations.literal: In Zhen'an there was a man named Jin who declared himself Jun's son.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhen'an a man named Jin claimed to be Jun's son.

sentences.zh: 鎮安土官乃潛召其舊部酋長，出金而與之盟曰：「若小主也。

translations.literal: The Zhen'an native official secretly summoned Jun's former subordinate chieftains, brought Jin out and made alliance with them, saying: "This is the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen'an native official secretly summoned Jun's old chieftains, presented Jin, and swore them to him: "This is your young lord.

sentences.zh: 」諸酋羅拜，擁金歸，聚兵五千，將攻城，復故地，遠近洶洶。

translations.literal: " The chieftains bowed in circles, escorted Jin back, gathered five thousand troops, were about to attack the city and recover the former territory; near and far were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: " The chiefs bowed in ranks, escorted Jin home, mustered five thousand men, and prepared to storm the city and recover the old domain. Alarm spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 浚誅時，其酋楊留者無所歸，率黨千余人詣賓州，應募為打手。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, his chieftain Yang Liu had nowhere to go; he led over a thousand followers to Bin Prefecture and enlisted as brawlers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was executed, his chief Yang Liu, left without a master, took more than a thousand followers to Bin Prefecture and enlisted as mercenary brawlers.

sentences.zh: 希儀在賓，留入言，欲往見小主人。

translations.literal: Xiyi was at Bin; Liu came in to speak, wishing to go see the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was stationed at Bin when Liu came to say he wished to visit the young lord.

sentences.zh: 希儀故患金，及聞留言，益大駭。

translations.literal: Xiyi had always been troubled about Jin, and on hearing Liu's words was all the more greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had already been worried about Jin; Liu's words filled him with dread.

sentences.zh: 因好謂留曰：「是岑浚第九子耶？

translations.literal: Thereupon he kindly said to Liu: "Is this Cen Jun's ninth son?
translations.idiomatic: He feigned delight and asked Liu, "Is this Cen Jun's ninth son?

sentences.zh: 我向征田州固聞之。

translations.literal: When I previously campaigned in Tianzhou I certainly heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: I heard as much when I campaigned in Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 」因自語：「岑氏其復乎？

translations.literal: " Thereupon to himself he said: "Will the Cen clan be restored?
translations.idiomatic: " Then, as if to himself: "So the Cen are to rise again?

sentences.zh: 」欲以深動留，留果喜。

translations.literal: " Wishing to deeply move Liu, Liu was indeed pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to stir Liu deeply—and Liu was pleased.

sentences.zh: 已，召留密室，言：「予我重賂，即為金復官。

translations.literal: Afterward he summoned Liu to a secret room and said: "Give me heavy bribes and I will restore Jin's office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he called Liu into a private room. "Pay me well," he said, "and I will restore Jin to office.

sentences.zh: 」且出，復呼入曰：「韋貴、徐五今分將思恩兵，必讎金，善防之。

translations.literal: " And as he went out, he called Liu back in and said: "Wei Gui and Xu Wu now divide command of Si'en's troops; they will certainly be Jin's enemies—guard against them well.
translations.idiomatic: " As Liu left, he called him back: "Wei Gui and Xu Wu now divide Si'en's troops between them. They will hate Jin—watch them closely.

sentences.zh: 」留益大信。

translations.literal: " Liu believed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu trusted him completely.

sentences.zh: 金遂從五千人因留以見。

translations.literal: Jin then came with five thousand men following Liu to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then came with his five thousand men, led by Liu, to an audience.

sentences.zh: 門者奔告，請無納。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper ran to report and requested that he not be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper ran in and begged that Jin not be admitted.

sentences.zh: 希儀罵曰：「金，土官子，非賊，奈何不納？

translations.literal: Xiyi cursed, saying: "Jin is a native official's son, not a bandit—why not admit him?
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi scolded him: "Jin is a native official's son, not a rebel—why turn him away?

sentences.zh: 」引入，厚結之，又引以詣兵備副使，隨以計漸散其五千人。

translations.literal: " He was led in, treated warmly and bound to him; he also led him to the vice military intendant, and by stratagem gradually dispersed his five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin was admitted, treated with honor, and presented to the vice military intendant; by degrees Xiyi's stratagem scattered the five thousand.

sentences.zh: 卒縛金，留亦自恨死，思恩復寧。

translations.literal: In the end Jin was bound; Liu also died of self-reproach, and Si'en was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jin was bound. Liu died of remorse, and Si'en was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 已，從總督張經大破斷藤峽、弩灘賊，受賚歸。

translations.literal: Afterward, following Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing he greatly defeated the bandits of Duan Gorge and Nubay, received an award of gifts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing in a great victory over the bandits of Duan Gorge and Nubay, received an imperial gift, and went home.

sentences.zh: 希儀鎮柳、慶久，渠魁宿猾捕誅殆盡。

translations.literal: Xiyi garrisoned Liu and Qing for a long time; ringleaders long entrenched in cunning were captured and executed almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had long held Liu and Qing in garrison. The ringleaders, hardened by years of raiding, were hunted down and executed almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 先後搗巢，斬馘積五千余級，未嘗悉奏功，故多不敘。

translations.literal: In successive nest-raids, severed heads accumulated to more than five thousand; he never fully reported merit in memorials, so much was not recorded in dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated raids on their strongholds he took more than five thousand heads, yet he never reported the full tally of his achievements, and much went unrecorded in the official dispatches.

sentences.zh: 十九年復謝病，柳人祀之山雲祠。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he again pleaded illness; the people of Liu erected a shrine to him at Shanyun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he again pleaded illness, and the people of Liuzhou enshrined him at the Shanyun Shrine.

sentences.zh: 旋起四川左參將，分守敘、滬及貴州迤西諸處。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Left Assistant Regional Commander of Sichuan, with divided duty guarding Xu, Hu, and the far-western districts of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as left assistant regional commander of Sichuan, with divided duty over Xu, Hu, and the western reaches of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其冬，擢署都督僉事，充總兵官，鎮貴州。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to Acting Regional Assistant Commander, appointed regional commander, and garrisoned Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to acting regional assistant commander, appointed regional commander, and posted to garrison Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 復謝病歸。

translations.literal: Again he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Once again he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 塞上多警，召天下名將至京師，希儀在召中。

translations.literal: The frontier was beset with many alarms; famous generals throughout the realm were summoned to the capital, and Xiyi was among those summoned.
translations.idiomatic: With alarms rising along the frontier, famous generals from across the realm were summoned to the capital, and Xiyi was among them.

sentences.zh: 希儀鎮柳、慶，每戰必先登，身數被創，陰雨輒痛劇，故數謝病。

translations.literal: When Xiyi garrisoned Liu and Qing, in every battle he was first to ascend; his body was wounded many times, and whenever it rained his pains grew severe, so he repeatedly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiyi held Liu and Qing, he was always first over the wall in battle. He was wounded again and again, and rainy weather would sharpen the pain, which is why he so often pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 至京，亦以病辭。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he also declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital he declined service on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其規避，褫都督官，令赴部候用。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected he was shirking duty, stripped him of regional commander rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry to await assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected him of evading duty, stripped him of his regional commander's rank, and ordered him to report to the ministry to await assignment.

sentences.zh: 翁萬達薦其才。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda recommended his ability.

sentences.zh: 會江、淮多盜，議設督捕總兵官，乃復希儀署都督僉事以往。

translations.literal: As Jiang and Huai had many bandits, it was proposed to establish a bandit-suppression regional commander; thereupon Xiyi was again made Acting Regional Assistant Commander and sent.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in Jiang and Huai, and the court proposed creating a bandit-suppression regional commander; Xiyi was again given acting regional assistant commander rank and sent there.

sentences.zh: 二十六年以為廣東副總兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was made Deputy Supreme Commander of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made deputy supreme commander of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 命自今將領至自川、廣、雲、貴者，毋推京營及西北邊，著為令。

translations.literal: An order was issued that henceforth generals arriving from Sichuan, Guang, Yun, and Gui should not be shifted off to the capital garrison or the northwest frontier; this was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that henceforth commanders arriving from Sichuan, Guangdong, Yunnan, and Guizhou were not to be shunted off to the capital garrisons or the northwest frontier—a rule thereafter kept in force.

sentences.zh: 從總督張嶽大破賀縣賊倪仲亮等，予實授，仍賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Following Governor-General Zhang Yue he greatly defeated the He County bandits Ni Zhongliang and others; he received formal appointment and was again granted silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor-General Zhang Yue he won a great victory over the He County rebels led by Ni Zhongliang and others. He received his commission in full rank and was again granted silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 瓊州五指山熟黎素畏法，供徭賦，知州邵浚虐取之。

translations.literal: The acculturated Li of Wuzhi Mountain in Qiongzhou had long feared the law and paid corvée and taxes; Prefect Shao Jun cruelly extorted from them.
translations.idiomatic: The acculturated Li of Wuzhi Mountain in Qiongzhou had long lived in awe of the law and paid their corvée and taxes. Prefect Shao Jun extorted from them with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 其酋那燕遂結崖州、感恩、昌化諸黎為亂。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Na Yan thereupon joined the Li of Yazhou, Gan'en, and Changhua in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief Na Yan then rallied the Li of Yazhou, Gan'en, and Changhua in revolt.

sentences.zh: 總督歐陽必進議並萬州、陵水黎討之，分兵五道。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ouyang Bijin proposed also punishing the Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui, dividing troops into five routes.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ouyang Bijin proposed also punishing the Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui, and divided his forces into five columns.

sentences.zh: 希儀適病，最後至，謂必進曰：「萬州、陵水黎未有黨惡之實，奈何並誅，益樹敵？

translations.literal: Xiyi happened to be ill and arrived last; he said to Bijin: "The Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui have no proven record of siding with the villains—why punish them together and only grow more enemies?
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi happened to be ill and arrived last. He told Bijin, "The Li of Wanzhou and Lingshui have no proven record of siding with the rebels. Why punish them along with the guilty and only breed more enemies?

sentences.zh: 莫若止三道。

translations.literal: Better to stop at three routes."
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave it at three columns."

sentences.zh: 」必進從之。

translations.literal: Bijin followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Bijin agreed.

sentences.zh: 希儀乃偕參將武鸞、俞大猷等直入五指山下，斬那燕及其黨五千四百有奇，俘獲者五之一，招降三千七百人。

translations.literal: Xiyi then together with Assistant Regional Commanders Wu Luan, Yu Dayou, and others went straight beneath Wuzhi Mountain; they beheaded Na Yan and his faction—five thousand four hundred odd in all; captives were one-fifth; three thousand seven hundred were persuaded to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi then joined Assistant Regional Commanders Wu Luan and Yu Dayou and others in a direct descent on Wuzhi Mountain. They killed Na Yan and more than five thousand four hundred of his followers, took one captive for every five killed, and persuaded three thousand seven hundred to surrender.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進都督同知，改貴州總兵官。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, he was advanced to Regional Vice Commander and transferred to regional commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the capital, he was promoted to regional vice commander and made regional commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 復從嶽平銅仁叛苗龍許保、吳黑苗。

translations.literal: Again following Yue he pacified the Tongren rebel Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao.
translations.idiomatic: Again following Zhang Yue he pacified the Tongren Miao rebels Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao.

sentences.zh: 又以病歸。

translations.literal: Again on grounds of illness he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Once again he went home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 倭寇海上，命督川、廣兵赴剿。

translations.literal: Japanese pirates raided the sea; he was ordered to supervise Sichuan and Guang troops to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates struck along the coast, he was ordered to lead Sichuan and Guangdong forces against them.

sentences.zh: 無功，為周如鬥劾罷。

translations.literal: Without achievement, he was impeached and dismissed by Zhou Rudou.
translations.idiomatic: He achieved nothing and was impeached and dismissed by Zhou Rudou.

sentences.zh: 希儀為人坦率，居恒謔笑，洞見肺腑。

translations.literal: Xiyi as a man was frank and open; in ordinary times he jested and laughed, yet his innermost thoughts were fully visible.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi was a frank and open man. In ordinary times he joked and laughed, yet everything in his heart showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 及臨敵，應變出奇，人莫測。

translations.literal: When facing the enemy he responded to change with surprise moves; no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came he adapted to circumstance with unexpected stratagems, and no one could read his next move.

sentences.zh: 尤善撫士卒。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at comforting soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Above all he knew how to win over his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 常染危病，卒多自戕以禱於神。

translations.literal: When he frequently fell gravely ill, many soldiers mutilated themselves to pray to the gods on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell gravely ill, many of his men would mutilate themselves in prayer to the gods for his sake.

sentences.zh: 最後一人，至以箭穿其喉。

translations.literal: The last man even drove an arrow through his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: One man, the last of them, drove an arrow through his own throat.

sentences.zh: 其得士心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the devotion he won from his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of devotion he commanded among his troops.

sentences.zh: 石邦憲，字希尹，貴州清平衛人。

translations.literal: Shi Bangxian, styled Xiyin, was a man of Qingping Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangxian, styled Xiyin, was a native of Qingping Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年嗣世職為指揮使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he inherited his hereditary post as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiajing reign he inherited his family's hereditary post as commander.

sentences.zh: 累功，進署都指揮僉事，充銅仁參將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was advanced to Acting Assistant Commander-in-Chief and appointed assistant regional commander of Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated victories he rose to acting assistant commander-in-chief and was made assistant regional commander of Tongren.

sentences.zh: 苗龍許保、吳黑苗叛，總督張嶽議征之，而賊陷印江、石阡，邦憲坐逮問。

translations.literal: The Miao Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao rebelled; Governor-General Zhang Yue proposed campaigning against them, but the bandits seized Yinjiang and Shiqian; Bangxian was arrested and interrogated on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao rebels Long Xubao and Wu Heimiao rose in revolt. Governor-General Zhang Yue proposed an expedition, but the rebels captured Yinjiang and Shiqian, and Bangxian was arrested and put under investigation.

sentences.zh: 嶽以銅仁賊巢穴，而邦憲有謀勇，乃奏留之。

translations.literal: Yue, because Tongren was the bandits' lair and Bangxian possessed strategy and courage, memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue knew Tongren was the rebels' stronghold and that Bangxian had both strategy and courage; he memorialized the throne to keep Bangxian in the field.

sentences.zh: 邦憲遂與川、湖兵進貴州，破苗砦十有五。

translations.literal: Bangxian then with Sichuan and Huguang troops advanced into Guizhou and broke fifteen Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian then advanced into Guizhou with Sichuan and Huguang troops and captured fifteen Miao stockades.

sentences.zh: 竄山箐者，搜戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Those who fled into mountain ravines were hunted down and slaughtered almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled into the mountain ravines were hunted down and slain almost to the last.

sentences.zh: 上功，邦憲第一。

translations.literal: Merit was reported; Bangxian ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was reported, Bangxian ranked first.

sentences.zh: 未及敘，而許保等突入思州，執知府李允簡以去。

translations.literal: Before rewards could be dispensed, Xubao and others suddenly entered Sizhou and seized away Prefect Li Yunjian.
translations.idiomatic: Before rewards could be issued, Xubao and his men suddenly broke into Sizhou and carried off the prefect Li Yunjian.

sentences.zh: 邦憲急邀，奪之歸。

translations.literal: Bangxian urgently intercepted them and recovered him.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian intercepted them in haste and brought the prefect back.

sentences.zh: 坐是停俸戴罪。

translations.literal: On account of this his salary was suspended and he served under demerit.
translations.idiomatic: For this his salary was suspended and he was ordered to serve while bearing the demerit.

sentences.zh: 賊既破思州，復糾余黨，與湖廣蠟爾山苗合，欲攻石阡。

translations.literal: The bandits having broken Sizhou, again rallied remnants and joined with the Huguang Miao of La'ershan, intending to attack Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: After sacking Sizhou the rebels rallied their scattered followers and joined forces with the La'ershan Miao of Huguang to attack Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 不克，還過省溪。

translations.literal: They failed to take it and on returning passed through Shengxi.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to take the city and, on their return march, passed through Shengxi.

sentences.zh: 千戶安大朝等邀之，斬獲大半，盡奪其輜重，賊不能軍。

translations.literal: Company Commander An Dachao and others intercepted them; more than half were beheaded or captured, all transport was seized, and the bandits could no longer maintain their army.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commander An Dachao and others cut them off, killing or capturing more than half their force and seizing all their baggage, until the rebels could no longer hold an army together.

sentences.zh: 邦憲乃使使購老穀、老犭革等執許保送軍門，而黑苗竄如故。

translations.literal: Bangxian then sent envoys to offer rewards that Lao Gu, Lao Ge, and others seize Xubao and deliver him to headquarters, while Heimiao fled as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian then sent agents to pay Lao Gu, Lao Ge, and others to seize Xubao and deliver him to headquarters, while Heimiao remained in hiding as before.

sentences.zh: 復以計購烏朗土官田興邦等斬黑苗，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Again by stratagem he paid Wulang native official Tian Xingbang and others to behead Heimiao; the bandits were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then paid the Wulang native official Tian Xingbang and others to kill Heimiao by stratagem, and the rebels were completely pacified.

sentences.zh: 遂進署都督僉事，充總兵官，代沈希儀鎮貴州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Acting Regional Assistant Commander, appointed regional commander, and replaced Shen Xiyi to garrison Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to acting regional assistant commander, appointed regional commander, and replaced Shen Xiyi as garrison commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 臺黎砦苗關保倡亂，四川容山、廣西洪江諸苗應之。

translations.literal: At Taili stockade the Miao chieftain Guanbao raised rebellion; the Miao of Rongshan in Sichuan, Hongjiang in Guangxi, and others responded.
translations.idiomatic: At Taili stockade the Miao chief Guanbao raised a revolt, and the Miao of Rongshan in Sichuan, Hongjiang in Guangxi, and other districts answered him.

sentences.zh: 遠近騷然，撫剿莫能定。

translations.literal: Near and far were in uproar; neither pacification nor suppression could settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm spread far and wide, and neither persuasion nor force could bring the situation under control.

sentences.zh: 邦憲與湖廣兵分道討破之，傳檄十八砦，許執首惡贖罪。

translations.literal: Bangxian with Huguang troops divided forces and campaigned to defeat them; he issued proclamations to eighteen stockades, permitting surrender of ringleaders to atone for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian divided his forces with Huguang troops and defeated the rebels, then sent proclamations to eighteen stockades offering amnesty to those who handed over the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 諸苗聽撫，設盟受約而還。

translations.literal: The various Miao submitted to pacification; after establishing alliance and accepting terms he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao submitted to pacification; once oaths were sworn and terms accepted, he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 播州宣慰楊烈殺長官王黼，黼黨李保等治兵相攻且十年，總督馮嶽與邦憲討平之。

translations.literal: Bozhou Surveillance Commissioner Yang Lie killed District Magistrate Wang Fu; Fu's faction Li Bao and others mustered troops and battled each other for nearly ten years; Governor-General Feng Yue with Bangxian campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lie, the Bozhou surveillance commissioner, killed District Magistrate Wang Fu. Fu's followers, led by Li Bao, mustered troops and fought one another for nearly ten years before Governor-General Feng Yue and Bangxian put them down.

sentences.zh: 真州苗盧阿項為亂，邦憲以兵七千編筏渡江，直抵磨子崖。

translations.literal: The Zhenzhou Miao chief Lu Axiang raised rebellion; Bangxian with seven thousand troops bound rafts, crossed the river, and went straight to Mozi Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenzhou Miao chief Lu Axiang rebelled. Bangxian took seven thousand men, built rafts, crossed the river, and drove straight to Mozi Cliff.

sentences.zh: 策賊必夜襲，先設備。

translations.literal: He anticipated the bandits would certainly night-raid and made preparations first.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the rebels would strike at night, he laid his traps in advance.

sentences.zh: 賊至，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the bandits came, he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When they came, he routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊求援於播州吳鯤。

translations.literal: The bandits sought aid from Bozhou's Wu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sought help from Wu Kun of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 諸將懼，邦憲曰：「水西宣慰安萬銓，播州所畏也。

translations.literal: The generals were afraid; Bangxian said: "Shuixi Surveillance Commissioner An Wanquan is what Bozhou fears.
translations.idiomatic: The other commanders grew fearful, but Bangxian said, "An Wanquan, the Shuixi surveillance commissioner, is the man Bozhou fears.

sentences.zh: 吾調水西兵攻烏江，聲楊烈縱鯤助逆罪，烈奚暇救人乎？

translations.literal: I will summon Shuixi troops to attack the Wujiang and proclaim Yang Lie's crime in letting Kun aid rebels—how would Lie have leisure to save anyone?"
translations.idiomatic: If I summon Shuixi troops against the Wujiang and charge Yang Lie with allowing Kun to abet rebellion, will Lie have any leisure to send relief?"

sentences.zh: 」已，水西兵至。

translations.literal: Before long Shuixi troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Shuixi troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 邦憲進逼其巢，乘風縱火，斬關而登，賊大奔潰，擒賊首父子，斬獲四百七十余人。

translations.literal: Bangxian advanced to press their lair; riding the wind he set fires, cut through the pass and ascended; the bandits fled in great rout; he captured the bandit chiefs, father and son; beheadings and captures exceeded four hundred seventy persons.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian pressed the rebel stronghold, set fires on the wind, broke through their gate, and stormed the heights. The rebels broke and fled. He captured the chief and his son, and took more than four hundred seventy heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 進署都督同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Regional Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting regional vice commander.

sentences.zh: 破地隆阡叛苗四砦，又破答千諸砦，擒其渠魁。

translations.literal: He broke four rebel Miao stockades at Dilongqian and also broke the stockades of Daqian and others, capturing their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed four rebel Miao stockades at Dilongqian, then broke the stockades at Daqian and elsewhere and captured their ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 地隆阡遺賊龍老三、龍得奎結龍停苗老夭、扳凳苗石章保等縱兵掠，執石耶洞土官妻冉氏以歸，攻梅平砦。

translations.literal: Remnant bandits at Dilongqian—Long Laosan, Long Dekui—joined Longting Miao Lao Yao, Bandeng Miao Shi Zhangbao, and others in raiding; they seized the wife surnamed Ran of the Shiyedong native official and carried her away, and attacked Meiping stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants at Dilongqian—Long Laosan and Long Dekui—joined the Longting Miao chief Lao Yao, the Bandeng Miao chief Shi Zhangbao, and others in raiding. They abducted the wife of the Shiyedong native official, a woman surnamed Ran, and attacked Meiping stockade.

sentences.zh: 官軍要擒老三。

translations.literal: The government troops intended to capture Laosan.
translations.idiomatic: The government forces set their sights on capturing Laosan.

sentences.zh: 得奎走免，復與老夭等攻破平南營囤。

translations.literal: Dekui escaped; again together with Lao Yao and others they broke the Pingnan camp depot.
translations.idiomatic: Dekui escaped, then joined Lao Yao and the others in storming the Pingnan camp depot.

sentences.zh: 邦憲偵冉氏在老夭所，陽議贖，而潛擊殺老夭。

translations.literal: Bangxian learned that Mistress Ran was in Lao Yao's hands; he openly negotiated ransom while secretly striking and killing Lao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mistress Ran was in Lao Yao's camp, Bangxian openly negotiated her ransom while secretly launching a raid that killed Lao Yao.

sentences.zh: 官軍遂入龍停砦，並執扳凳砦苗龍老內，令執獻章保。

translations.literal: The government troops then entered Longting stockade and also seized the Bandeng stockade Miao Long Laonei, ordering him to seize and present Zhangbao.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops then entered Longting stockade and also seized Long Laonei of Bandeng stockade, ordering him to capture Zhangbao and deliver him up.

sentences.zh: 於是諸苗悉降。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the Miao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the Miao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 白洗、養鵝諸苗叛，討擒其魁，降百余砦。

translations.literal: The Miao of Baixi, Yang'e, and others rebelled; he campaigned and captured their chiefs; more than a hundred stockades surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Baixi and Yang'e Miao and others rebelled; he defeated them, captured their chiefs, and brought more than a hundred stockades to surrender.

sentences.zh: 湖廣漵浦瑤沈亞當等為亂，總督石勇檄邦憲討之，生擒亞當，斬獲二百有奇。

translations.literal: The Huguang Xupu Yao Shen Yadang and others raised rebellion; Governor-General Shi Yong dispatched Bangxian to suppress them; he captured Yadang alive; beheadings and captures exceeded two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Xupu Yao of Huguang, led by Shen Yadang, rose in revolt. Governor-General Shi Yong ordered Bangxian against them; he captured Yadang alive and took more than two hundred heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 漵浦甫平，銅仁、都勻苗相煽叛。

translations.literal: Xupu had barely been pacified when Tongren and Duyun Miao incited one another in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xupu had barely been pacified when the Miao of Tongren and Duyun stirred one another to rebel.

sentences.zh: 邦憲亟馳還，率守備安大朝進剿。

translations.literal: Bangxian urgently galloped back and led Garrison Commander An Dachao in advance to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian raced back at once and led Garrison Commander An Dachao in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 先破彪山砦賊，乘勝略定諸砦。

translations.literal: First he broke the bandits of Biaoshan stockade; riding victory he generally pacified the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He first broke the rebels at Biaoshan stockade, then rode the momentum to bring the other stockades under control.

sentences.zh: 獲賊首龍老羅、王三等，余黨盡平。

translations.literal: He captured bandit chiefs Long Laoluo, Wang San, and others; the remaining faction was completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the rebel chiefs Long Laoluo, Wang San, and others, and the last of their followers were pacified.

sentences.zh: 又與總督黃光升，修湖北墩臺、烽堠百十所，招降冷水溪諸洞苗二十八砦。

translations.literal: Again with Governor-General Huang Guangsheng he repaired more than a hundred and ten beacon platforms and watch mounds in Hubei, and persuaded twenty-eight stockades of Cold Water Creek and other cave Miao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Governor-General Huang Guangsheng, he restored more than a hundred and ten watch platforms and beacon mounds in Hubei and persuaded twenty-eight stockades of the Cold Water Creek cave Miao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 播州容山副長官土舍韓甸與正長官土舍張問相攻，甸屢勝，遂糾生苗剽湖、貴境，垂二十年。

translations.literal: Bozhou Rongshan Deputy District Magistrate native cadet Han Dian and Principal District Magistrate native cadet Zhang Wen attacked each other; Dian repeatedly won, then rallied raw Miao to plunder the Huguang and Guizhou frontiers for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dian, the Bozhou Rongshan deputy district magistrate, and Zhang Wen, the principal district magistrate, fought one another. Dian won again and again and then rallied unpacified Miao to raid the Huguang and Guizhou frontier for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 問亦糾黨自助。

translations.literal: Wen also rallied a faction to aid himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wen in turn rallied allies of his own.

sentences.zh: 邦憲討之，斬百余人。

translations.literal: Bangxian campaigned against them and beheaded more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian campaigned against them and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 問潛出，被獲。

translations.literal: Wen slipped out secretly and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wen slipped out in secret and was captured.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘勝入甸巢。

translations.literal: The government troops, riding victory, entered Dian's lair.
translations.idiomatic: Riding their victory, government troops entered Dian's stronghold.

sentences.zh: 會暮，大雨，迷失道。

translations.literal: At evening it happened to rain heavily and they lost the way.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a heavy rain fell and they lost the trail.

sentences.zh: 守備葉勛、百戶魏國相等陷伏中，死焉。

translations.literal: Garrison Commander Ye Xun, Company Commander Wei Guoxiang, and others fell into an ambush and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Ye Xun, Company Commander Wei Guoxiang, and others walked into an ambush and were killed.

sentences.zh: 邦憲奪圍出，還軍鎮遠。

translations.literal: Bangxian fought out of the encirclement and returned the army to Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian fought his way out and withdrew to Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 再征之，賊沿江守。

translations.literal: Campaigning against them again, the bandits defended along the river.
translations.idiomatic: On a second expedition the rebels held the river line.

sentences.zh: 邦憲佯與爭，而別自上流三十里編竹以渡。

translations.literal: Bangxian feigned contention while separately from upstream thirty li he bound bamboo to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian feigned a contest for the crossing while, thirty li upstream, his men bound rafts of bamboo and slipped across.

sentences.zh: 水陸並進，大破之。

translations.literal: By land and water advancing together, he greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked by land and water at once and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 斬甸，容山平。

translations.literal: Dian was beheaded; Rongshan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dian was beheaded, and Rongshan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進右都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 邦憲生長黔土，熟苗情。

translations.literal: Bangxian grew up in Qian soil and knew Miao conditions well.
translations.idiomatic: Bangxian had grown up in Guizhou and knew the Miao country intimately.

sentences.zh: 善用兵，大小數十百戰，無不摧破。

translations.literal: Skilled in employing troops, in large and small battles numbering tens and hundreds, none failed to be crushed.
translations.idiomatic: A master of arms, he fought scores and hundreds of engagements large and small without once failing to break the enemy.

sentences.zh: 前後進秩者四，賚銀幣十有三。

translations.literal: In all he was advanced in rank four times and granted silver and silks thirteen times.
translations.idiomatic: In all he was promoted four times and granted silver and silks on thirteen occasions.

sentences.zh: 所得俸賜，悉以饗士，家無贏資。

translations.literal: All salary and grants received he entirely used to feast soldiers; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he earned in salary and gifts he spent on his men; his household held no surplus.

sentences.zh: 為總兵官十七年，威鎮蠻中。

translations.literal: Serving as regional commander for seventeen years, his authority awed the barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: For seventeen years as regional commander his authority held the entire frontier in awe.

sentences.zh: 與四川何卿、廣西沈希儀並稱一時名將。

translations.literal: Together with He Qing of Sichuan and Shen Xiyi of Guangxi he was acclaimed as famous generals of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He stood with He Qing of Sichuan and Shen Xiyi of Guangxi among the age's finest generals.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈左都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of left commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：嗚呼，明至中葉，曷嘗無邊材哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: Alas, when Ming reached its middle period, when was it ever without frontier talent!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Alas—down to the mid-Ming, when was the dynasty ever truly bereft of men of frontier genius?

sentences.zh: 如馬永、梁震、周尚文、沈希儀之徒，出奇制勝，得士卒死力，雖古名將何以加焉？

translations.literal: Men such as Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, Zhou Shangwen, and Shen Xiyi, by striking with surprise to gain victory and winning the troops' willingness to die for them—how could even the famous generals of antiquity surpass them?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Ma Yong, Liang Zhen, Zhou Shangwen, and Shen Xiyi won by surprise and mastery of the field and commanded their soldiers' utmost loyalty—what ancient famous general could have done more?

sentences.zh: 然功高賞薄，起蹶靡常。

translations.literal: Yet their merit was high while rewards were thin, and their rises and falls were never constant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their achievements were great while their rewards were meager, and their fortunes rose and fell without steady pattern.

sentences.zh: 此無異故，其抗懷奮激，無以結歡在朝柄政重人，宜其齟齬不相入也。

translations.literal: This is not for no reason: their proud, ardent spirits could not win favor with the powerful men who held sway at court, and it was fitting that they should clash and fail to fit in.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is plain: their proud, impassioned temperaments could not curry favor with the powerful men who held the reins at court, and so it was only to be expected that they would chafe against them and never find a place.

sentences.zh: 馬芳三代為將，父子兄弟先後殉國，偉矣哉！

translations.literal: The Ma Fang family produced generals for three generations; father, sons, and brothers in succession died for the state—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Ma Fang family served as generals; fathers, sons, and brothers in turn gave their lives for the state—how magnificent!
